summary: TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE pass via jq --arg and accept empty silently — the counters' --argjson hard-stop has no equivalent
description: #58 explicitly out of scope. The same status-write blocks that pass the counter via --argjson (which hard-fails on an empty value: 'invalid JSON text passed to --argjson', exit 2) pass TEST_VERDICT / TEST_SCOPE via --arg, which accepts empty silently — an unsubstituted verdict writes verdict:"" into status.jsonl rather than failing the step. These are legitimately model judgments and #58 keeps verdict interpretation in the orchestrator, so this is not a counter problem; it is the same substitution assumption with a quieter failure mode. Affected sites include bkit-build.md:538/:612/:936, bkit-debug.md:400/:643/:756, bkit-ship.md:562/:625/:685.
remediation: Validate the verdict against the PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS vocabulary inside the write block (case "$V" in PASS|FAIL|CONCERNS) ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac) so an unsubstituted verdict routes to the Failure Path instead of writing an empty string into the log; or move the verdict through --argjson with an enum-validating jq filter.

summary: PRIOR_STRATEGY folds status.jsonl with ALL-runs scoping; whether a resumed run should restart the STANDARD->PIVOT->FINAL ladder was never established
description: #58 flagged but did not change this. PRIOR_STRATEGY (bkit-build.md:592 and :987, bkit-debug.md:624, bkit-ship.md:665) reads [.[] | .steps[] | select(...)] | last.strategy — .[] spans ALL runs. Verified: given a completed run that recorded PIVOT and a fresh second run with no diagnose rows of its own, the shipped read returns PIVOT; an active-run-scoped read returns empty. #58 scopes its attempt derivation to the ACTIVE run — deliberately OPPOSITE — because cross-run counting would hand a resumed workflow the previous run's attempts and starve its budget immediately (the starvation DE-25 had to fix for SOAK). Both sites now carry a comment naming the asymmetry, since it looks like a bug from either direction. What strategy actually wants was not established: a resumed run arguably should NOT restart the ladder from scratch, which would make the all-runs read correct.
remediation: Decide the intended resume semantics for strategy, then either scope the read to the active run (matching the attempt derivation) or record the cross-run behaviour as intentional in .bkit/workflows.md § Status so the asymmetry stops reading as an oversight.

summary: No CI gate runs shellcheck over .bkit/scripts/*.sh — actionlint only shellchecks run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*
description: Discovered while planning #58. The shipped shell surface (.bkit/scripts/bkit-counter-bus.sh, bkit-counter-bus-config.sh, bkit-slop-delta.sh, bkit-protect-main.sh, bkit-set-dependabot.sh, and #58's new bkit-status-fold.sh) is sourced by consumers under sh/dash/zsh but is linted by nothing: the bkit-tests-static lane runs actionlint, which shellchecks only the run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*. The SC2016 disable #58 adds to bkit-status-fold.sh (the fold blob's $w/$e/$i are jq variables, not shell) is therefore defensive for local runs only. A real POSIX-portability regression in a shipped script would land green and only surface in a consumer's shell.
remediation: Add a shellcheck -s sh step over .bkit/scripts/*.sh to the bkit-tests-static lane (and the .bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/*.sh sources). Scope to the shipped scripts, not the whole repo, and pin the shellcheck version the way actionlint is pinned.

summary: The 'start a new run?' test keys on the last run overall, not the last run of THIS workflow — an interleaved debug run can silently reset a resuming build's attempt budget
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. bkit-build.md:335 tests (.[-1] // {}) — the last folded run of ANY workflow — to decide whether to append a fresh workflow-started row. build and debug write to the SAME docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl. So if a debug run interleaves and completes between two build invocations, a resuming build sees .[-1].workflow == 'debug', appends a fresh workflow-started, and starts a NEW active run — resetting its attempt budget. #58 makes active-run scoping the basis of every counter, which promotes this from latent to load-bearing: it is Defect 3 (fresh budget on resume) through a side door, reachable via the exact build->debug->build path the feature governs. A lock exists at bkit-build.md:143; whether it excludes the interleave is NOT established. #58 characterises current behaviour in tests/counter-derive.bats (T2.10) so the dependence is visible rather than latent, but does not change the boundary.
remediation: Decide the intended run-boundary semantics and key the test on the last run OF THE SAME WORKFLOW (e.g. [.[] | select(.workflow==$w)] | last) rather than .[-1], or establish and document that the bkit-build.md:143 lock makes the interleave impossible. Belongs with #209's status.jsonl substrate, not with #58's control-flow slice. Read T2.10's characterisation assertion first — it records what today actually does.

summary: debug-run-tests writes its step-done row with no commit (KN-26 removed it), so NORMAL_ATTEMPT's row counting depends transitively on Steps 4/5/6 advancing parentSha
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58 counts step-done rows and dedups on 'S {workflow} {step} {parentSha} {at}'. build-run-tests commits --allow-empty per attempt (bkit-build.md:939), so its parentSha advances by itself. debug-run-tests does NOT (bkit-debug.md:396 reads 'Update status:' with no commit — the only step-done-writing step in debug without one). That asymmetry is KN-26's remediation: a chore(...) commit as branch HEAD makes the Vercel-ignore regex skip the preview, CI demotes to partial, integration/Playwright are skipped, and the run reports conclusion=success with no coverage. So NORMAL_ATTEMPT's attempts stay distinct only via Steps 4/5/6's commits (bkit-debug.md:573/:646/:707) advancing parentSha, plus the dedup key's 'at' second. Whether debug-run-tests SHOULD regain a commit — making its row counting self-sufficient — is a real design question that collides with KN-26 and must not be settled by an implementer applying #58's per-site shape. #58 pins the current shape with a corpus audit (T2.6) that requires each counted step to either commit in-block or sit on a commented transitive-exemption list.
remediation: If debug-run-tests's transitive parentSha dependency proves fragile, resolve it WITHOUT re-adding a chore(...) commit — e.g. amend the dedup key, or have the step commit under a subject the Vercel-ignore regex does not match. Any change must be reviewed against KN-26's full failure chain first. Do not simply delete the T2.6 exemption entry.

summary: The 5 close-workflow counter emitters declare counterName DESIGN_ATTEMPT/PLAN_ATTEMPT/BUILD_ATTEMPT/... but #58 derives counterValue from the workflow-started count — the pairing is unverified
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. #58's T7.1 replaces --argjson counterValue 1 (a hardcoded literal labelled model-self-report) with a fold-derived all-runs count of workflow-started events for that workflow, and flips counterSource to shell-bus. That makes the VALUE honest — it is a real number the shell counted. Whether that number is what each emitter's declared counterName means is a separate question #58 does not adjudicate: the names (DESIGN_ATTEMPT, PLAN_ATTEMPT, BUILD_ATTEMPT, ...) suggest an invocation index, which the workflow-started count is, but this was asserted rather than established against #234's schema intent. Flagged so the value/name pairing is not quietly assumed correct by the next reader of stats.jsonl.
remediation: Settle alongside #234's counterSource enum question ('derived' vs 'shell-bus' — which names the transport rather than the provenance). Confirm each emitter's counterName denotes an invocation index; if any denotes something else, either rename it or derive a different value for that emitter. #234 owns the schema.

Both the pragmatic and optimal-tradeoff lenses independently identified full kernel extraction as the correct two-year shape, and it was rejected for this cycle only because it would design function boundaries against semantics still being decided in the same change, and because it creates a second source of truth plus a version-skew hazard between installed scripts and rendered markdown. Once 384 lands, the contract is defined and the extraction becomes mechanical.

description: 384 ships the hole detector as a fail-open advisory with a pinned watermark and a delta report, matching the bkit comply rollout, because the existing corpus is 25-65% holey across consumer-a and consumer-b and a day-one aggregate gate would emit hundreds of findings and be muted within a week. The expected step set is derived from bkit-ship.md rather than a parallel table, so the contract tracks the workflow automatically. Promotion to a blocking gate is the intended end state but requires the delta baseline to be clean first.
remediation: once the delta against the pinned watermark stays clean for a release across the consumer repos, flip the detector to exit non-zero on new holes and wire it into bkit check

summary: remove ships writable checkout of feat/{FID} entirely except inside the B2 conflict window, so bookkeeping-never-moves-the-head becomes unreachable rather than remembered
description: The risk-premortem lens proposed making the invariant structural: ship runs from the dev tree plus gh API calls and never holds a writable feat/{FID} checkout outside B2. Rejected for 384 because the evidence inverts its premise - B2 (same-line doc collisions on long-lived branches) is the common case, not the escape hatch, so the approach concentrates all remaining worktree usage in the path exercised most and tested least while every other path loses its checkout and its diagnosability. Its two strongest findings (scope Step 12 removal to run-created worktrees, and state the invariant as push timing rather than tree location) are absorbed into 384 as decisions. Revisit only after 384s gate has run in production and if B2 gains real conflict-resolution coverage.
remediation: if revisited: sequence after the merge gate exists and is proven, scope Step 12 to ownership first, keep the push-timing formulation, and add a vitest invariant asserting no git commit or git push targets feat/{FID} outside the B2 block

summary: define a recovery path for a shipped-but-wrong workflow change - consumers pin @cbartens/bkit and receive workflows on bkit upgrade, with no per-workflow revert
description: Surfaced by the 384 risk premortem as a cross-cutting gap rather than a 384 defect. Consumers receive .bkit/workflows via bkit upgrade at a pinned package version; there is no mechanism to revert a single workflow file to a prior known-good version without downgrading the whole package, which also reverts unrelated fixes. If a new ship merge gate is wrong, the recovery path for three consumer repos is currently undefined. 384 mitigates locally with a single logged override (BKIT_SHIP_GATE_OVERRIDE recorded as a status.jsonl row), but that is a per-run escape, not a rollback.
remediation: design a per-workflow pin or revert affordance for bkit upgrade (e.g. a .bkitignore-style per-file version pin, or bkit upgrade --revert <workflow> restoring the prior canonicalHash), and document the recovery runbook in docs/deployments.md

This mirrors Sub-Plan 5's precedent (Manual Verification Step 5, debug-egress loudness) of leaving a live-only step deliberately unchecked rather than fabricating completion.

Once run, check the corresponding boxes in `docs/plans/202607/341-three-runtimes-plan-6.md` Manual Verification section.

summary: Marker-primary FID reorder (D9) elevates untrusted PR-body input for filesystem path construction with no documented slug validation
description: docs/plans/202607/logs/341-three-runtimes/build-challenge.md finding F4: bkit-auto.md steps 9-10 (D9 reorder) make the PR-body marker <!-- bkit:fid={FID} --> the PRIMARY FID source, ahead of the feat/-derived branch fallback. Per docs/security.md section CI Auto-Route Trust, the PR body is only collaborator-trusted (triage/write, not commit-signed). FID subsequently flows into filesystem paths (docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/..., .worktrees/{FID}) with no documented validation that it is a bare slug (no / or ..), so a marker like bkit:fid=../../elsewhere could redirect status/worktree writes outside the intended log directory. Classed architectural (touches the FID-resolution contract consumed across all five phase workflows, not a single mechanical file fix) -- deferred rather than remediated in this build-challenge pass per protocol (architectural findings are not fixed inline).
remediation: Validate the parsed FID against a strict slug allowlist (e.g. ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, rejecting / and ..) before it builds any path, in the same step it is extracted (bkit-auto.md step 9). Record the constraint alongside the marker-trust text in docs/security.md section CI Auto-Route Trust. Apply consistently across every workflow that consumes FID for path construction.

summary: Marker-primary FID reorder (D9) elevates untrusted PR-body input for filesystem path construction with no documented slug validation

remediation: Slug allowlist enforced at resolution site per docs/security.md CI Auto-Route Trust.

The PR-merge branch (mode 3) has no non-live coverage at all — it needs an actual claude.ai session to confirm the PR create/merge, the auto-delete-head-branches cleanup, and the adopt-mode worktree skip.
remediation: Before merge: run one real /bkit-design or /bkit-plan cycle on the laptop and confirm the close lands docs({FID}): ... DONE bkit [skip ci] on dev with no CI run dispatched, and that ship completes with a dirty dev tree (the AHEAD_NON_SKIP path). After merge: run one phase from a claude.ai cloud session and confirm the PR-path close.

summary: Do not fold #384 into #341 — sequence ship redesign after runtime-aware close lands
description: #384 (Path A read-only resume / Path B integrate-then-revalidate, one capstone gate, bookkeeping on the dev tree) layers on #341 rather than conflicting. #341 makes ship runtime-aware (where the tree is, whether RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES); #384 makes ship head-stable (what may move the PR head). One interaction: #384 says bookkeeping never rides the feature branch — status.jsonl/ship artifacts go to the dev tree from Step 1 — but a cloud runtime cannot write the dev tree. Express that as: write to the dev tree when RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true, else to the current branch. Folding #384 into #341 would re-open the local-path byte-identity question this PR closed.
remediation: Land #341 first. Then design/plan #384 with the RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES-conditioned bookkeeping rule already available.

summary: GitHub merge queue (rebase onto base, CI on merge_group, server-side merge if green) is unavailable to bkit consumers — private + non-Enterprise; would require a merge_group trigger in every consumer ci.yml
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. A GitHub merge queue would make the merge gate server-side (rebase onto base, run CI on the merge_group event, auto-merge if green) and remove the head-movement race bkit-ship-gate.sh exists to close. Unavailable: bkit consumer repos (consumer-a, consumer-b) are private and on a non-Enterprise plan; merge_group is an Enterprise/Beta feature gated behind plan tier. Adopting it would require every consumer ci.yml to add a merge_group trigger and the repos to upgrade their plan — a cross-consumer policy change, not a ship-workflow decision.
remediation: revisit only if the consumer plan tier changes (private repos gain merge queue access); record the plan-tier gate in docs/deployments.md alongside the merge-gate contract when revisited

summary: Required status checks on dev via bkit-protect-main.sh (closing the UI hand-merge path) — separable additive cross-consumer policy with its own plan-tier question; deferred from #384 ship gate
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. bkit-protect-main.sh already makes bkit-tests-check the sole required check on main. Extending required-status-checks enforcement to dev (so a human cannot UI-merge a PR whose capstone is not green, closing the gap bkit-ship-gate.sh closes on the agent path) is a separable additive policy. It has its own plan-tier question: branch protection on private repos is plan-gated (the REST protection/ruleset APIs return 403 on cbartens/bkit today — see docs/deployments.md § Autonomous phase-close prerequisites), so the enforcement cannot be verified mechanically on every consumer. Out of scope for #384 because the agent-driven gate (bkit-ship-gate.sh) is the load-bearing assertion; UI-merge prevention is defence-in-depth, not the contract.
remediation: future issue: extend bkit-protect-main.sh to dev (or a ruleset) and document the plan-tier prerequisite; pair with per-workflow-rollback-path-for-shipped-bkit-workflow-changes if that affordance lands first

summary: Mode-3 (cloud, RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) BOOK_ROOT live-verification is not exercised in #384 E2E validation — both validated paths are local-mode (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true). Prose contract mechanically asserted by Tier-2 invariant (bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts BOOK_ROOT conditional presence check, 14/14 GREEN) and ship-failure-path.bats case 2. Live E2E deferred to first mode-3 ship run.
reason: Mode-3 cloud runtime (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) is not available in the build session — requires a cloud agent (Claude Code cloud / Cursor cloud) executing a ship workflow. The #341 three-runtimes feature introduced the RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES flag but its live verification is itself still OPEN.

summary: Second /bkit-audit synthesis correlation rule (derived-divergence-candidate) joining derived-data dual-source-writer with reliability unchecked-write on one subject — deliberately not shipped in 4.11.0
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror. The A4 correlation rule table ships exactly one rule (silent-corruption-candidate). derived-data emits a dual-source-writer signal in 4.11.0 that no rule consumes, so the signal is emitted-but-unjoined. A second rule is new probe behaviour rather than reconciliation, and one rule already proves the mechanism and exercises the unevaluable coverage path on the bkit dogfood run.
remediation: after one real /bkit-audit run has produced a dual-source-writer signal, add one row to the rule table in bkit-audit.md Step 6 plus the derived copy in bkit-audit-synthesise.md; the four-way parity assert keeps the two copies honest

summary: The /bkit-audit severity x class matrix was designed at 11 lenses; at 18 it flattens — maintainability alone carries 7 lenses — and WS-D (#207) makes it worse
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror. 18 lenses map onto 7 finding classes, so the matrix loses discriminating power: architecture, debt, dead-code, docs-drift, logic-dupe, ui-ux and reference-signal all land in maintainability. Accepted for 4.11.0; the per-class appendix is the escape valve for a human reader. Introducing a sub-class axis is a report-shape change, out of scope for a reconciliation pass.
remediation: decide during WS-D (#207) design, which adds the web-product lens family and compounds the flattening; either accept the flat matrix permanently or introduce a sub-class axis once, not per workstream

summary: No audit-{token} skills exist in the public registry, so /bkit-audit Step 4 (skill install) will mostly no-op — whether bkit authors a minimal seed set is unowned
description: Pass-4 design out-of-scope mirror, carried unresolved from Pass 3. The stack-detect + skill-install enrichment model is the mechanism by which stack-specific depth reaches the stack-agnostic lens prompts, but the registry has no audit-{token} skills to install. The non-gating posture absorbs this and the audit runs to full strength on universal probes regardless, so it is a latent value gap rather than a blocker. Pass 3 routed this to docs/pending.md, which no longer exists — hence the orphan.
remediation: after the first real /bkit-audit runs, decide whether bkit authors a minimal seed set of audit-{token} skills or leaves the surface to the community; either way record the decision rather than carrying it as a design open question a fourth time

summary: Reconciler/sweeper to recover a ship displaced out of the depth-1 GHA concurrency queue
description: GHA holds exactly one pending run per concurrency group; a third concurrent ship displaces the pending second. That PR stays green, open and merge-ready but never ships, and the displaced run executes no step so no bkit-authored notice, comment, label or ledger row can exist for it. #397 restates requirement 1 as met for N=2 only and accepts the N>=3 hole this cycle, because the allowlist ship discriminator removes the dominant eviction source (green dev CI entering the ship lane). The automated fix is an idempotent reconciler: sweep for green bkit:auto PRs with no in-flight ship and re-dispatch, riding the post-merge dev CI trigger #363 adds (which fires exactly when the ship lane frees).
remediation: future issue after #397 lands: bump cloud job permissions to actions: write; cap the sweeper hard (max one dispatch per sweep, reuse #363's MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS bounding); make the admission probe and the sweep predicate call ONE shared implementation, not two similar gh run list invocations; keep the predicate stack-agnostic (workflow filename, never a consumer-editable CI display name). Belongs with #260's single-flight/idempotent-dispatch substrate.

summary: Split bkit-cloud.yml into a light router plus a single-trigger-surface executor workflow — the deferred target shape for multi-producer dispatch
description: #397 records this as the right long-term shape and rejects it for this cycle. bkit-cloud.yml keeps both trigger surfaces but becomes a router (checkout + resolve, ending in gh workflow run bkit-cloud-run.yml -f phase -f fid -f arg); the new executor has ONE trigger surface with ONE payload shape, so its concurrency group is a literal string and the cross-surface same-FID gap stops existing rather than being closed. It is also the natural dispatch primitive #260 (milestone workstreams) and #324 (audit findings) both want to consume: adding a producer becomes adding a caller, not editing a concurrency expression. Rejected now as net-new shipped infra (new workflow file, manifest entry, template, advisory, actions: write bump, two-hop latency, doubled Actions run count) for a problem two expressions plus a resolver job cover.
remediation: revisit when #260 and #324 add the second and third dispatch producers; at that point #397's expression work becomes the thing this replaces. A dropped or 403 re-dispatch is a silent no-op for a whole phase, so the router needs its own dispatch-verify.

summary: External cross-runner mutex (orphan git ref or issue-label compare-and-swap) as a real distributed single-flight lock
description: #397 rejects this for its own scope. The file locks (.bkit/.dev.lock, docs/plans/*/logs/{FID}/.lock) are gitignored and runner-local, so they arbitrate nothing across GHA runners. A primitive that does survive would be a compare-and-swap on a dedicated orphan ref (git push origin <sha>:refs/bkit-locks/ship-global — GitHub ref creation is server-atomic) or an issue-label CAS tolerating the 422 as lock-held, with age-based stale reaping mirroring today's 30-min-idle rule. It closes both gaps without depending on any inferred GHA behaviour. Rejected because it introduces a DURABLE state surface whose lock survives a hard-killed runner with no guaranteed reaper (an if: always() step can still be skipped on hard cancellation) — a worse blast radius than an ephemeral file lock that vanishes with the VM — and because it would leave two independent lock layers to reconcile.
remediation: revisit only if #260's single-flight lock / leader election requirement lands first and wants to share a primitive; design the reaper before the acquirer.

summary: With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY both set, one bkit-cloud run launches two agents that both dispatch /bkit-auto against the same PR
description: The claude and opencode jobs are additive by design and documented as such in the bkit-cloud.yml header: both fire on the same event when both secrets are present. They are ONE run, so workflow-level concurrency cannot separate them by construction — a ship-global lane delivers one ship RUN at a time, not one ship AGENT at a time. Two agents then race on the same feat/{FID} branch and the same PR, backstopped only by gh pr merge --match-head-commit. #397 leaves this exactly as today: its job-level FID lanes are suffixed per agent (-claude / -opencode) precisely so the additive contract is not silently converted into a queue with its own eviction hazard. Pre-existing, not introduced by #397, and simultaneously an intended feature and an unarbitrated same-FID collision.
remediation: future issue: decide whether additive dual-agent execution is still wanted post-#397; if yes, scope it to non-mutating phases or give the two agents disjoint worktrees; if no, make the jobs mutually exclusive at the secret-gate step rather than via a shared concurrency group.

summary: Nothing detects that the cloud egress allowlist pasted into a Claude/Cursor dashboard is stale relative to what bkit generates
description: cloud.md renders a paste block a human copies into a vendor dashboard. When bkit's derived host set changes (new provider, new MCP host) the dashboard keeps the old value and the only symptom is an opaque harness timeout on the model call, not a network error. No surface can compare intended to actual because the allowlist lives in a web UI. #381 ships a stable fingerprint line in the paste block as the cheap half of the mitigation; detection is out of scope.
remediation: future issue: have the cloud bootstrap hook echo the expected allowlist fingerprint (and optionally probe reachability of one provider host) so a mismatch is visible in the cloud run log

summary: OpenCode curl/wget allowlist is a command substring glob, so an allowlisted domain in a query param or header defeats the host check Cursor now enforces
description: injectOpencodeNetworkCurlAllows writes permission.bash entries of the form 'curl *{base}*' (bkit-modules.ts:1706-1714). OpenCode's permission model is a command glob, so 'curl https://evil.tld/?x=z.ai' matches and is allowed, while the Cursor hook rejects it (host-parsed since #394) and Claude has no shell curl gate at all. #381 widens the base list and therefore widens this asymmetry; it documents the weaker guarantee in .bkit/providers.md rather than fixing it, because OpenCode exposes no URL-host permission primitive.
remediation: future issue: revisit if OpenCode gains a host-based permission primitive or a pre-tool hook comparable to Cursor beforeShellExecution; until then keep the limitation stated in providers.md

summary: One generated allowlist artifact read at runtime by all three IDE surfaces is blocked by the Claude and OpenCode permission schemas, not by bkit design
description: The theoretical ideal is a single JSON artifact (tooling defaults + all registry hosts + consumer allowed-domains) that every surface reads at runtime, collapsing BKIT_SHIPPED_NETWORK_DOMAINS, the Cursor hook list and the WebFetch allow entries into reads of one file. Cursor already works this way via .cursor/allowlist.json. Claude permissions.allow requires a literal WebFetch(domain:...) string per host and OpenCode permission.bash requires a literal command glob per host, neither has a file-reference primitive, so the work would land for 1 of 3 surfaces. Recorded so it is not re-proposed without re-discovering the constraint.
remediation: revisit only if Claude Code or OpenCode ships a file-referenced permission source; most of the maintenance win is already captured by deriving the source list in #381

summary: The opencode provider key set is still mirrored by hand into four lists plus two doc tables, each held together only by a keep-in-sync comment
description: #381 removes the domain-list duplication but not the key-set duplication: OPENCODE_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS (bkit-modules.ts:1397) is mirrored by OPENCODE_PROVIDERS + OPENCODE_PROVIDER_ALIASES (bkit-cli.ts:43-74), OPENCODE_PROVIDER_COLUMN (bkit-install.ts:320), EFFORT_COLUMN_FOR_PROVIDER (bkit-install.ts:436), and the Models tables in .bkit/prompts.md and .bkit/providers.md. bkit-cli.ts:40 carries the same 'keep in sync with ...' comment pattern #381 exists to remove, and no test asserts key-set parity. Out of scope for #381, which is scoped to egress hosts.
remediation: future issue: derive the CLI allowlist and the display/effort column maps from the registry moved to .bkit/src/bkit-registry.ts by #381, and add a key-set parity test over every mirror

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers API-contract conformance — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded, and invisible once Pass 2 became historical
description: Pass 2 (bar-199-audit-workflow-design.md) deferred an api-contracts lens on the argument that structural source probes have poor signal-to-noise without a live surface to diff against. Pass 3 said nothing about it and Pass 4 folded no probe for it, so the 18-lens inventory silently has no coverage of published-interface breakage, schema drift between producer and consumer, or endpoint contract regressions. The defer is still the right call — the gap is that the RATIONALE stopped being visible the moment Passes 2 and 3 were reclassified as historical and the Pass-4 doc became the sole input to /bkit-plan. That is the same failure shape that lost the WS-1..WS-8 decomposition when sub-issues 187-193 and 208 were deleted.
remediation: do NOT add a lens without first reading this row — it has now been deferred twice on the same signal-to-noise argument. Candidate home is WS-E (#83) once runtime evidence exists and a real surface can be diffed, or a conditional lens gated on a new hasPublicApi flag authored in WS-C. Not 4.11.0.

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers rate limiting / abuse throttling — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded
description: Pass 2 deferred a rate-limiting lens alongside api-contracts on the same argument. Pass 4 carries no probe for request throttling, quota enforcement, backoff on retry paths, or abuse surfaces, and the security lens (B9) is chartered to hunt permissive holes in auth, validation, secrets and data exposure rather than request-rate policy. Verified absent under every synonym (rate-limit, throttl, quota, backoff, abuse). The defer stands: detecting a MISSING rate limit needs request-path modelling that a static grep-shaped lens does not do, and a false negative here reads as a clean security pass.
remediation: candidate homes are WS-E (#83, once a live surface can be probed) or an amendment to security (B9) — but only with a probe that can distinguish absent-limit from limit-enforced-at-a-layer-not-in-this-repo, otherwise it emits confident false negatives on exactly the class it exists to catch. Not 4.11.0.

summary: derived-data (C3) absorbs only the CONSISTENCY half of Pass-2 deferred caching lens — TTL, invalidation, stampede and key-cardinality remain uncovered by all 18
description: Pass 2 deferred a caching lens. Pass 4 introduces derived-data (C3, gated on hasDerivedStore), which covers cache CONSISTENCY: single-authoritative-writer, every source-mutation path updating the derived store, and whether any test or store constraint asserts the two agree. It does NOT cover cache CORRECTNESS or EFFICIENCY: TTL policy, invalidation strategy, stampede / thundering-herd protection, or key-cardinality blowup. The risk is a reader treating the Pass-2 caching defer as fully resolved because a cache-shaped lens now exists, when only one half was absorbed — the partial absorption is easy to mistake for a complete one.
remediation: if the caching half is wanted, it is an amendment to derived-data (C3) rather than a new lens — same hasDerivedStore gate, same subject identity — but it changes the lens from a consistency derivation into a policy scan, so decide deliberately rather than by accretion. Not 4.11.0.

summary: main branch excluded from the bkit-cloud workflow_run trigger — a documented REVERSAL of #363 pivot-comment D-final, which settled the branch filter as [feat/**, fix/**, dev, main]
description: #363's pivot comment (2026-07-22) D-final explicitly listed 'verify at both dev (post-merge) and main (post dev->main promotion)' with a routing table and diff both including main. The plan (v3/v4) moved main to Out of Scope instead, and this build ships without it. Rationale: the issue's own open item 3 never resolved 'routing on main only works if the promotion commit carries the marker; bkit has no consumer-facing dev->main promotion workflow, so confirm where that commit is authored (may be out of bkit's control for some consumers)' -- with no bkit-authored promotion commit to thread bkit [auto route] onto, a main trigger would be gated shut by construction for exactly the consumers it targets. A follow-up comment (2026-07-29) additionally locked bkit:auto as dev-only by policy: dev->main promotion and any merge into main always requires explicit human interaction, matching the existing hard-stop after Ship (docs/comparison.md).
remediation: revisit only if/when a bkit-authored dev->main promotion workflow exists that could carry the bkit [auto route] marker on the promotion commit; until then main stays workflow_dispatch-only (manual)

summary: MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS cap is enforced from status.jsonl on origin/dev, a file the dispatched /bkit-debug session itself has contents:write to rewrite — the cap is self-resettable by the principal it bounds
description: bkit-cloud.yml documents MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS=3 as a cost/security control bounding a stuck dev/fix/** feedback loop, but the counter it reads (dev-dispatch rows in docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl on origin/dev) is the same file every dispatched /bkit-debug session legitimately edits every run, with contents:write. Any actor or malfunctioning/prompt-injected agent that can push to dev can rewrite or drop those rows, silently restoring the remaining-attempts budget to 3 and continuing the failure->debug->push->failure cycle indefinitely. The fail-closed push-verification added for #363 P6 protects only against under-counting from lost pushes, not against an authorized rewrite.
remediation: Derive the count from a source the dispatched session cannot rewrite — e.g. gh run list --workflow bkit-cloud.yml filtered by FID, or an append-only tracker comment/label written with a token the dispatched session does not hold — or minimally cross-check the file-derived count against gh api run history and take the maximum before dispatching. This is a new counter architecture, not a mechanical patch, so it was deferred rather than attempted in the build-challenge-remediate pass.

summary: docs/plans/** artifacts still quote the pre-sweep headings and internal labels; the shipped-docs guard deliberately excludes them
description: Five 363 build-log artifacts quote `## Post-merge dev CI auto-routing (#363)` verbatim, and plan/design docs across docs/plans/ carry issue refs and retired ledger keys throughout. bkit-shipped-docs-refs.test.ts scans only the manifest corpus plus the docs/ payload, so the archived tree is out of scope by design.
remediation: leave archived artifacts alone unless they start being read as current doctrine — they are phase records, and rewriting them destroys the audit trail the ship bookkeeping depends on. If a sweep is ever wanted, scope it to headings only and never to the finding bodies.

summary: providers.md keeps dated live-probe stamps, which read as history but carry the staleness signal for a model pin
description: The internal-identifier sweep removed issue refs and history framing from providers.md but kept lines like `zai` live-proved 2026-07-27 and `moonshot` still base-URL/env-verified. Under a strict current-state-only reading these are history; operationally they are the only signal telling a reader how stale a pin verification is.
remediation: Obsolete: the providers it tracked (zai, moonshot) were removed from the opencode allowlist, and the dated probe stamps went with them.

summary: workflows.md § /bkit-auto still describes Steps 1-4 with a Stale-Run Guard and Opt-In Gate; the shipped workflow has Step 1 + Step 2 only
description: The section documents a four-step orchestrator (2 = Stale-Run Guard, 3 = Opt-In Gate, 4 = Dispatch). The shipped .bkit/workflows/bkit-auto.md has two steps — Start Workflow and Dispatch — because the guard and the opt-in gate moved into bkit-cloud.yml ctx step. The arg-shape and mode rows were corrected for the CI_DEV mode but the step table itself was not, so a reader following it looks for steps that do not exist. Predates this cycle.
remediation: re-cut the § /bkit-auto step table against the shipped file, and state where the guard and gate actually live (bkit-cloud.yml ctx step) rather than listing them as orchestrator steps.

summary: The 363 plan still lists the 4.10.0 -> 4.11.0 bump as a task, so a re-run re-applies what this cycle reverted
description: Plan task T12 and its execution checklist instruct bumping package.json and .bkit/version pinnedVersion, calling the bump a forward-only release tag. The bump was reverted and the rule recorded (version-bump-belongs-to-the-release-commit), but the plan is an archived artifact and was left unedited, so any resume or replay of that plan reintroduces it.
remediation: no edit to the archived plan; the durable guard is the decision row plus the release procedure. If plan replay ever becomes routine, teach the plan template that version bumps are release-commit-only.

summary: jsonl.md lists workflow and step as required envelope fields, but manually-authored rows have no phase to name
description: Three live rows omit workflow (one also omits step): docs/decisions.jsonl and docs/knowledge.jsonl rows carrying step manual-investigation, and one docs/failures.jsonl row. The field table in .bkit/jsonl.md marks workflow and step as required (no ? suffix, unlike subagent? and model?), so the schema and the data disagree. bkit-ledger-integrity.test.ts therefore gates ts/kind/repo/bkitVersion only — backfilling a phase name would put invented data in a ledger that feeds the analysis pass.
remediation: pick one: mark workflow/step optional in the jsonl.md field table for manually-authored rows, or define an explicit sentinel (workflow: manual) and backfill the three rows, then widen the gate in bkit-ledger-integrity.test.ts to cover both fields.

summary: Mode-3 (cloud, RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) BOOK_ROOT live-verification is not exercised in the ship bookkeeping E2E validation — both validated paths are local-mode (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true)
description: Prose contract is mechanically asserted by the Tier-2 invariant (bkit-ship-invariants.test.ts BOOK_ROOT conditional presence check) and ship-failure-path.bats case 2, but the live path is unexercised. Blocker: mode-3 requires a cloud agent (Claude Code cloud / Cursor cloud) executing a ship workflow, which is not available in a local build session; the three-runtimes RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES live verification it depends on is itself still OPEN. Supersedes the same-key row that carried this prose in a free-text reason field, no description, lowercase severity, a friction-only scope field, a non-schema dependsOn field and ts 0.
remediation: verify on the first mode-3 ship run: assert BOOK_ROOT resolves to the main checkout and the bookkeeping commit lands there, then close this row

summary: no width reduction for bkit-build Step 10 challenge-1/-2 or Step 11 challenge-reconcile
description: bkit-build Step 10 runs two adversarial challengers carrying different dimensions (bugs / security), so dropping -2 deletes security coverage outright rather than trimming a duplicate. Step 11 challenge-reconcile stays unconditional as a direct consequence: with both challengers always running there are always two reports to merge, so a 'skip when only one ran' condition never fires. Sensitive-path globs may only force challenge width up, never reduce it.
remediation: none wanted — revisit only if a future lens split makes one challenger genuinely redundant

summary: bkit-build Step 4 build-plan-current stays unconditional
description: The obvious skip is 'the plan commit is an ancestor of the base', but Step 2 branching off a stale origin/dev is exactly the case this step exists to catch — the candidate predicate would disable the guard on its own failure mode. Dropped from the candidate list by the issue's own audit.
remediation: none wanted

summary: no step-count reductions in bkit-debug or bkit-ship
description: Every subagent-invoking step in both workflows is already conditional — debug on DEBUG_MODE and TEST_VERDICT, ship on the base path and the merge state. Ship is the merge gate and stays maximally strict regardless of task size. Both workflows still receive the step-skipped logging retrofit; only their conditions are untouched. Debug's one accepted change is the entry-routing rule, which is in scope for this plan.
remediation: none wanted

summary: extend the status-hole detector beyond ship to design / plan / build / debug
description: bkit-status-hole-detector.ts models ship only: a frozen canonical step order, four path classifications (PATH_A / PATH_B / MERGED_ON_ENTRY / ABORTED) and per-path mandatory sets, all derived from bkit-ship.md. Once step-skipped rows exist across all five workflows the detector could read skips from the log instead of inferring them from absence, which is the strongest available argument for promoting it from advisory to gate. Plan-sized rather than mechanical: each of the other four workflows needs its own routing-branch model (debug's NORMAL/SOAK ladder and attempt loops, build's verify/challenge retry loops, plan's SPLIT branch, design's SPIKE and MILESTONE branches), a corpus sweep to seed each expected set from real runs, and a per-workflow fail-open-to-gate promotion policy — new machinery in a new module surface, not an edit to the existing one.
remediation: design a per-workflow path model + expected-set derivation, seed each from a status.jsonl corpus sweep, then promote per workflow behind its own fail-open window

references: #442 § Net new machinery for the whole issue
summary: no scale dial, no skip-precondition prose enum, no human approval gate on escalation, no new workflow
description: Explicitly rejected by the issue's agreed approach, which caps net new machinery at step-skipped rows, per-lens applicability predicates and one escalation verdict. A NARROW|STANDARD|WIDE dial collapses independent facts into one number and lets filename numbering pick the surviving lens; a second skip-precondition enum in workflow prose would duplicate the decidedBy enum already on the row; a human approval gate would sit on escalation, the one direction that cannot be abused.
remediation: none wanted

summary: applicability predicates for design Step 3 ideate-2 (optimal-tradeoff) and ideate-3 (risk premortem)
description: Both lenses are candidates in the issue's audit, but Step 3 is the first subagent-invoking step in bkit-design and its only input is the raw issue text in design-input.md — there is no upstream artifact to carry a predicate and no bash-countable signal. Decision needed between: (A) keep all three ideate lenses unconditional and drop them from scope, forgoing a two-invocation saving on bug-fix-shaped designs but adding no machinery and risking no silent loss of the risk lens; (B) split Step 3 into two waves — run ideate-1 alone, have it emit LegacyConstraint and NewRuntimeSurface flags, then conditionally fan out -2 and -3, which needs no new agent but serialises a step that is parallel today so the full-width path pays wall-clock; (C) add a cheap pre-Step-3 classifier subagent emitting both flags, which keeps the fan-out parallel but is net-new machinery the issue ruled out and spends one invocation to maybe save two. Plan recommends A and applies it as the default.
remediation: pick A, B or C at the plan's Gate 1 confirmation; only B and C reopen this as implementation work

summary: Applicability predicate for /bkit-plan Step 9 complexity-check
description: #442 asks for a predicate that skips complexity-check when SPLIT is unreachable. The published rule is SINGLE = estimated tokens <= 85K AND task count <= 12. Task count is greppable; the token estimate is a model judgement with no artifact behind it, so a task-count predicate cannot prove the token arm unreachable. .bkit/stats.jsonl holds 12 outcome rows; taskCount is 0 on every design/plan row and 55, 55, 55, 92, 119, 119, 129 on build/ship rows, with no datapoint between 1 and 54 - zero calibration for the low end. Step 9 therefore stays unconditional and carries no skip arm and no COMPLEXITY_VERDICT hard-set.
remediation: Revisit once .bkit/stats.jsonl carries outcome rows with taskCount between 1 and 54. Then either calibrate a task-count threshold against real small-plan rows, or add a token-estimate artifact the predicate can read.
source: plan review merge - Open Question 6, option A

summary: Amend plan template Design-Missing Fallback for standalone plans

summary: One vocabulary for conditional-lens outcomes across workflows and audit
description: Two surfaces are converging on the same idea with different names. The workflow side introduces a step-skipped status row with a closed decidedBy enum (caller-flag / upstream-verdict / applicability) to make a deliberately skipped lens distinguishable from a crashed one. The audit side ships a three-state coverage manifest (ran / N-A-not-applicable / crashed) plus an applicability-override marker for the same false-all-clear problem, and its own review found that the override escape hatch is textually indistinguishable from genuine absence. Decision needed: do the two share one vocabulary, or stay separate? Options: (a) one shared enum plus one shared row type, read by both surfaces - highest consistency, largest blast radius across shipped workflows and audit prompts; (b) keep both, document the mapping in one place - cheapest, but two names for one idea persist; (c) align only the enum member names, leave the carriers separate - middle cost, removes the naming divergence without touching either carrier.
remediation: Decide before both surfaces ship. If (a) or (c), pick the canonical member names first, then retrofit whichever surface lands second.

summary: Drift gate over the rendered host mirrors
description: The rendered agent and command mirrors under .claude, .cursor and .opencode are force-overwritten and untracked by the drift check, so bkit check exits 0 while a mirror is stale against its source. A source edit that is never re-rendered therefore ships silently, and agents act on the stale rendered copy. Plan-sized rather than a mechanical fix: it needs a per-host render-output model (what each host emits for a given source, including the prune set), a decision on whether force-overwritten output can be drift-gated at all without fighting the overwrite, and a fail-open to gate promotion policy so the first release does not block on pre-existing drift.
remediation: Model the render output per host, add a drift comparison for it, and land it fail-open for one release before promoting to a gate.

summary: bkit upgrade does not write .bkit/advisories.md, so an advisory raised on the upgrade path has no durable artifact

summary: emptying the settings.json WebFetch seed leaves enrich-added grants behind on bkit uninstall, because they are no longer template-scoped
description: #381 empties the WebFetch(domain:...) block from .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json (it was a stale partial subset covering only 7 of 10 shipped bases in wildcard form). .claude/settings.json uninstall uses stripTier2JsonScope against the manifest template, so with the seed empty the grants enrichClaudeSettingsWebFetch wrote are outside the template scope and are left in the consumer's file after uninstall. A real consequence of emptying the seed, disclosed rather than papered over. PLAN-SIZED because the uninstall decision matrix is format-driven (fully-managed, markered-text, byte-equal-text, json) and this adds a fourth axis, provenance, which every format branch and the heavy-customised-consumer round-trip byte-identity fixture must be re-reasoned against; it is the same class of change as the prune itself, on a different verb.
remediation: future issue: make uninstall provenance-aware by reading .bkit/version webFetchDerived (the record #381 introduces) and stripping exactly the strings bkit recorded writing, leaving hand-added grants untouched; the mechanism now exists, the uninstall decision matrix does not yet consume it

summary: bkit uninstall deletes derived WebFetch grants by recomputing resolveNetworkAllowlist, so it cannot distinguish a hand-added grant that collides with a derived base
description: Corrected premise, verified against source 2026-08-26. .bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts:583-598 recomputes resolveNetworkAllowlist(ctx.cwd).map((d) => `WebFetch(domain:${d})`) at :589 and folds it into templateDoc.permissions.allow BEFORE stripTier2JsonScope, so enrich-added grants were never scoped to the .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json seed and emptying that seed strands nothing. The real gap is the inverse: uninstall deletes by RECOMPUTATION rather than by provenance, so any permissions.allow entry matching the CURRENT derived set is treated as bkit-owned and removed, including one the consumer added by hand. #381 widens the derived set from 10 to 15 bases (githubcopilot.com, models.dev, npmjs.org, skills.sh, tavily.com), widening that strip scope by 10 entries. PLAN-SIZED because the uninstall decision matrix is format-driven (fully-managed, markered-text, byte-equal-text, json) and consuming provenance adds a fourth axis that every format branch and the heavy-customised-consumer round-trip byte-identity fixture must be re-reasoned against; it is the same class of change as #381's WebFetch prune, on a different verb.
remediation: future issue: read .bkit/version webFetchDerived (the record #381 introduces) in bkit-uninstall.ts instead of recomputing resolveNetworkAllowlist at :589, and strip exactly the strings bkit recorded writing; add a round-trip integration case asserting a hand-added non-derived grant survives bkit uninstall claude while derived grants do not

summary: OpenCode permission.bash curl/wget allow globs are never revoked on any verb, so a dropped allowed-domains entry keeps its shell egress grant forever
description: injectOpencodeNetworkCurlAllows (.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1726-1734) assigns bash[`curl *${base}*`] = allow and bash[`wget *${base}*`] = allow for every resolved base and deletes nothing, on install or upgrade. The injected keys are absent from the rendered template, so stripTier2JsonScope leaves them on uninstall too. A consumer who removes a domain from .agents/context.md allowed-domains loses WebFetch(domain:<d>) via #381's prune and keeps curl *<d>* and wget *<d>* permanently: a shell egress grant strictly broader than the WebFetch grant that was revoked. #381 adds ten more such keys per consumer (five new bases x curl + wget) and does not close this. Distinct from 381-opencode-curl-glob-substring-bypass, which covers the glob SHAPE (a query parameter defeats the substring match) and not the LIFECYCLE. PLAN-SIZED because closing it needs a second provenance record for .opencode/opencode.json with no .bkit/version analogue today, a second recording contract mirroring #381's dryRun and non-writing-path rules, and an uninstall interaction of its own on a surface that install merges rather than rewrites.
remediation: future issue: give .opencode/opencode.json the same previous-minus-current prune #381 gives .claude/settings.json, recording the injected glob keys in .bkit/version alongside webFetchDerived; or define one revocation contract every egress surface implements and assert it with a single cross-surface parity test

summary: Codex has no read-tier gate: private-key deny and .env ask are unenforced there, because the Codex file-read tool name is unverified
description: The Codex guardrail is registered on the shell tool (Bash) only. The other three hosts also gate READS -- deny on .pem/.p12/id_rsa, ask on .env and .env.* -- and Codex does not, so on that host an agent can read private-key material and secrets with no gate at all. The blocker is that the hook matcher keys on tool_name and the Codex docs consulted confirm only Bash as a tool name; the file-read tool name was not established. Registering a guessed matcher is worse than leaving it: the hook installs, exits 0 and silently never fires, which is a gate that proves only that it was asked for. The read-gates block in bkit-permissions-parity.integration.test.ts is scoped to claude/opencode/cursor for this reason.

That asymmetry is KN-26's remediation: a chore(...) commit as branch HEAD makes the Vercel-ignore regex skip the preview, CI demotes to partial, integration/Playwright are skipped, and the run reports conclusion=success with no coverage. So NORMAL_ATTEMPT's attempts stay distinct only via Steps 4/5/6's commits (bkit-debug.md:619/:700/:773) advancing parentSha, plus the dedup key's 'at' second. Whether debug-run-tests SHOULD regain a commit — making its row counting self-sufficient — is a real design question that collides with KN-26 and must not be settled by an implementer applying #58's per-site shape. The current shape is pinned by a corpus audit (.bkit/src/bkit-counter-prose-audit.test.ts:248 TRANSITIVE_EXEMPTIONS) that requires each counted step to either commit in-block or sit on the transitive-exemption list.
remediation: If debug-run-tests's transitive parentSha dependency proves fragile, resolve it WITHOUT re-adding a chore(...) commit — e.g. amend the dedup key, or have the step commit under a subject the Vercel-ignore regex does not match. Any change must be reviewed against KN-26's full failure chain first. Do not simply delete the TRANSITIVE_EXEMPTIONS entry (.bkit/src/bkit-counter-prose-audit.test.ts:248).

summary: No CI gate runs shellcheck over .bkit/scripts/*.sh — actionlint only shellchecks run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*
description: Discovered while planning #58. The shipped shell surface (.bkit/scripts/bkit-counter-bus.sh, bkit-counter-bus-config.sh, bkit-slop-delta.sh, bkit-protect-main.sh, bkit-set-dependabot.sh, and #58's new bkit-status-fold.sh) is sourced by consumers under sh/dash/zsh but is linted by nothing: the bkit-tests-static lane runs actionlint, which shellchecks only the run: blocks inside .github/workflows/*. The SC2016 disable #58 adds to bkit-status-fold.sh (the fold blob's $w/$e/$i are jq variables, not shell) is therefore defensive for local runs only. A real POSIX-portability regression in a shipped script would land green and only surface in a consumer's shell.
remediation: Add a shellcheck -s sh step over .bkit/scripts/*.sh to the bkit-tests-static lane (and the .bkit/templates/.bkit/scripts/*.sh sources). Scope to the shipped scripts, not the whole repo, and pin the shellcheck version the way actionlint is pinned.

summary: GitHub merge queue (rebase onto base, CI on merge_group, server-side merge if green) is unavailable to bkit consumers — private + non-Enterprise; would require a merge_group trigger in every consumer ci.yml
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. A GitHub merge queue would make the merge gate server-side (rebase onto base, run CI on the merge_group event, auto-merge if green) and remove the head-movement race `bkit runs gate` (.bkit/src/commands/workflow/runs.ts:1368) exists to close. Unavailable: bkit consumer repos (consumer-a, consumer-b) are private and on a non-Enterprise plan; merge_group is an Enterprise/Beta feature gated behind plan tier. Adopting it would require every consumer ci.yml to add a merge_group trigger and the repos to upgrade their plan — a cross-consumer policy change, not a ship-workflow decision.
remediation: revisit only if the consumer plan tier changes (private repos gain merge queue access); record the plan-tier gate in docs/deployments.md alongside the merge-gate contract when revisited

summary: Required status checks on dev via `bkit setup protect-main` (closing the UI hand-merge path) — separable additive cross-consumer policy with its own plan-tier question; deferred from #384 ship gate
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. `bkit setup protect-main` (.bkit/src/commands/setup/setup.ts:39, BRANCH = "main") already makes bkit-tests-check the sole required check on main; its header (setup.ts:6-8) states dev is left unprotected on purpose — operators choose direct-push or feat/PR. Extending required-status-checks enforcement to dev (so a human cannot UI-merge a PR whose capstone is not green, closing the gap `bkit runs gate` closes on the agent path) is a separable additive policy. It has its own plan-tier question: branch protection on private repos is plan-gated (the REST protection/ruleset APIs return 403 on cbartens/bkit today — see docs/deployments.md § Autonomous phase-close prerequisites), so the enforcement cannot be verified mechanically on every consumer. Out of scope for #384 because the agent-driven gate (`bkit runs gate`, .bkit/src/commands/workflow/runs.ts:1368) is the load-bearing assertion; UI-merge prevention is defence-in-depth, not the contract.
remediation: future issue: extend `bkit setup protect-main` (.bkit/src/commands/setup/setup.ts) to dev (or a ruleset), reconciling the setup.ts:6-8 'dev left unprotected on purpose' stance, and document the plan-tier prerequisite; pair with per-workflow-rollback-path-for-shipped-bkit-workflow-changes if that affordance lands first

summary: TEST_SCOPE is written as a free-form `--field=scope=` and accepts empty silently — TEST_VERDICT is now enum-checked by `bkit steps done`, scope has no equivalent
description: #58 explicitly out of scope. Status writes now go through `bkit steps done`, which rejects an empty or out-of-enum --verdict with exit 2 (.bkit/src/commands/workflow/steps.ts:251-254), closing the TEST_VERDICT half. TEST_SCOPE still passes as a generic `--field=scope=...` row field with no validation, so an empty substitution writes scope:"" into status.jsonl and exits 0 (verified 2026-10-09 against `bkit steps done --field=scope=""`). Affected sites: .bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md:395, .bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:642, .bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:1120. The scope value originates from `bkit tests run` output (.bkit/src/commands/workflow/tests.ts:134) and reaches the write block through an agent-substituted placeholder.
remediation: Validate scope inside `bkit steps done` (or give it a dedicated flag that refuses empty) so an empty/unsubstituted scope routes to the Failure Path instead of writing an empty string into the log; or pipe `bkit tests run`'s scope straight into the write block without an agent-substituted placeholder.

summary: OpenCode curl/wget allowlist is a command substring glob, so an allowlisted domain in a query param or header defeats the host check Cursor now enforces
description: injectOpencodeDerivedAllows writes permission.bash entries of the form 'curl *{base}*' (bkit-modules.ts:1899-1911). OpenCode's permission model is a command glob, so 'curl https://evil.tld/?x=z.ai' matches and is allowed, while the Cursor hook rejects it (host-parsed since #394) and Claude has no shell curl gate at all. #381 widens the base list and therefore widens this asymmetry; it documents the weaker guarantee in .bkit/providers.md rather than fixing it, because OpenCode exposes no URL-host permission primitive.
remediation: future issue: revisit if OpenCode gains a host-based permission primitive or a pre-tool hook comparable to Cursor beforeShellExecution; until then keep the limitation stated in providers.md

summary: bkit upgrade does not write .bkit/advisories.md, so an advisory raised on the upgrade path has no durable artifact
description: writeAdvisoriesArtifact is called only from the doctor branch (bkit-install.ts:1871) and the install/check path (bkit-install.ts:2749); the upgrade branch returns without it. #381 adds a webfetch-grants-pruned advisory naming the exact WebFetch(domain:...) strings it removed, so on upgrade only two of the three recording destinations apply: the console line and git diff .claude/settings.json. This is a general install/upgrade finalisation-parity gap that pre-dates #381 and affects every advisory, not just the prune's. PLAN-SIZED because closing it means restructuring where the upgrade branch finalises and flushes ctx.advisories, not adding a call at the existing return: the install path builds its finding set through runPostInstallCheck, which upgrade never enters, so the fix is a new shared finalisation seam plus its cross-verb parity coverage.
remediation: future issue: restructure the upgrade branch's finalisation so it flushes its findings through the same runPostInstallCheck plus writeAdvisoriesArtifact path install uses, then assert parity with an integration test that raises one advisory on each verb

summary: bkit uninstall deletes derived WebFetch grants by recomputing resolveNetworkAllowlist, so it cannot distinguish a hand-added grant that collides with a derived base
description: Corrected premise, verified against source 2026-08-26. .bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts:550-562 recomputes resolveClaudeDerivedAllows(ctx.cwd) at :556 and folds it into templateDoc.permissions.allow BEFORE stripTier2JsonScope, so enrich-added grants were never scoped to the .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json seed and emptying that seed strands nothing. The real gap is the inverse: uninstall deletes by RECOMPUTATION rather than by provenance, so any permissions.allow entry matching the CURRENT derived set is treated as bkit-owned and removed, including one the consumer added by hand. #381 widens the derived set from 10 to 15 bases (githubcopilot.com, models.dev, npmjs.org, skills.sh, tavily.com), widening that strip scope by 10 entries. PLAN-SIZED because the uninstall decision matrix is format-driven (fully-managed, markered-text, byte-equal-text, json) and consuming provenance adds a fourth axis that every format branch and the heavy-customised-consumer round-trip byte-identity fixture must be re-reasoned against; it is the same class of change as #381's WebFetch prune, on a different verb.
remediation: future issue: read .bkit/version claudeAllowDerived (the record #381 introduces) in bkit-uninstall.ts instead of recomputing resolveClaudeDerivedAllows at :556, and strip exactly the strings bkit recorded writing; add a round-trip integration case asserting a hand-added non-derived grant survives bkit uninstall claude while derived grants do not

summary: OpenCode permission.bash curl/wget allow globs are never revoked on any verb, so a dropped allowed-domains entry keeps its shell egress grant forever
description: injectOpencodeDerivedAllows (.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1899-1911) assigns bash[`curl *${base}*`] = allow and bash[`wget *${base}*`] = allow for every resolved base and deletes nothing, on install or upgrade. The injected keys are absent from the rendered template, so stripTier2JsonScope leaves them on uninstall too. A consumer who removes a domain from .agents/context.md allowed-domains loses WebFetch(domain:<d>) via #381's prune and keeps curl *<d>* and wget *<d>* permanently: a shell egress grant strictly broader than the WebFetch grant that was revoked. #381 adds ten more such keys per consumer (five new bases x curl + wget) and does not close this. Distinct from 381-opencode-curl-glob-substring-bypass, which covers the glob SHAPE (a query parameter defeats the substring match) and not the LIFECYCLE. PLAN-SIZED because closing it needs a second provenance record for .opencode/opencode.json with no .bkit/version analogue today, a second recording contract mirroring #381's dryRun and non-writing-path rules, and an uninstall interaction of its own on a surface that install merges rather than rewrites.
remediation: future issue: give .opencode/opencode.json the same previous-minus-current prune #381 gives .claude/settings.json, recording the injected glob keys in .bkit/version alongside claudeAllowDerived; or define one revocation contract every egress surface implements and assert it with a single cross-surface parity test

summary: Adopt release-PR mirror mode in bkit's own bkit-ci so a promotion PR reuses the dev push run
description: bkit's own bkit-ci re-runs the full suite on a release/* -> main promotion PR whose head is a commit the dev push run already tested green: PR #527 run 38150872681 (release/5.0.1 -> main, head 6f3ce659) duplicated dev push run 38150686541 (same head, 3 min earlier, run_level=full). The release-PR mirror mode that fixes this already exists (docs/deployments.md One CI run per dev commit; decision release-pr-mirrors-dev-push-run; template scaffold .bkit/templates/.github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml) but is not enabled in .github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml, and its head_ref == dev predicate does not match bkit's release/* promotion flow. Check SHA Cache cannot cover it: on a pull_request event github.sha is the synthetic merge commit (395fffec) while gh run list reports the real head, so the headSha match never fires. Enabling it needs Decide Release Mirror in bkit-tests-scope, a Mirror Push Run capstone step (that job has no checkout or install today), the predicate widened to dev plus release/**, and the merged-PR -> light arm dropped so every dev push is full (mirror precondition 1). Plan-sized: it changes the run-level contract, the capstone, and the promotion path.
remediation: Plan the CI contract change: widen the mirror predicate to release/**, drop the merged-PR -> light arm in Decide Run Level, add Decide Release Mirror plus Mirror Push Run to .github/workflows/bkit-ci.yml, then update docs/deployments.md One CI run per dev commit. Issue #528 carries the evidence, preconditions, open questions and acceptance criteria.

summary: Replay a real run — animate a run's own status.jsonl instead of the scripted walkthrough
description: #504 later-idea 1. Read a run's status.jsonl and animate what actually happened (which agents ran, what review flagged, where it looped back) rather than the scripted stable skeleton. Real traps: a run that crashed with no final row, rows out of order, overlapping timestamps from parallel agents. Cost: it reads bkit's log format, so it must change whenever that does — it is a real bkit feature reading status.jsonl, not a demo fixture.
remediation: not this cycle; if revisited, design it as a bkit feature whose versioned contract is the status.jsonl row format

summary: A "your repo" report built from the user's own GitHub data via gh api
description: #504 later-idea 2. A local script runs gh api against the user's repo (gh works from the throwaway copy; no need to run inside their real repo) and writes a git-ignored data.js — not .json, because a page opened from disk cannot load JSON — so a token never reaches a web page. Analyses ranked: issues ready for bkit (biggest value add: it turns the demo into their first real use), CI health, where PR time goes, hotspots. Real traps: bot PRs (Dependabot) counted as people, GitHub's 30-result default silently shortening 'last year' to three weeks, reverted PRs counted as successes, empty or brand-new repos crashing the charts. Constraints: the benchmark would need a recorded snapshot instead of live data, and a user's data must never appear in anything published.
remediation: not this cycle; needs a Linear path (Linear issues are not on GitHub) and a recorded snapshot for benchmark use

description: #504 later-idea 3. For returning users only (a new user has no bkit runs): compare PRs made through bkit with the rest on their own data. This is the honest version of a time-saved calculator because it is measured on their work. Must be shown as a comparison, not 'bkit saved you X', since bkit tends to be used on different kinds of work than the rest.
remediation: not this cycle; needs recorded runs before the comparison is meaningful

Parsing a diff has real traps: renamed files, binary files, Windows line endings. A cost estimate could be added once the benchmark has measured real runs; until then it describes, it does not estimate.
remediation: not this cycle; the estimate half is blocked on measured run costs

summary: Publish the latest benchmark-built demo for people deciding whether to use bkit
description: #504 later-idea 7. On each release, the benchmark run builds the demo fresh; if it passes, publish it labelled with the bkit version that built it, and keep the run's paper trail alongside (design doc, plan, PR with the reviewer's comments and the fix), because that is what a careful evaluator wants to inspect. The blocker as written is stale: it assumes the package is on GitHub Packages with access: 'restricted', but @cbartens/bkit is public on npmjs today. For the public it needs a separate public repo (e.g. cbartens/bkit-demo) with GitHub Pages — GitHub shows committed HTML as source code, not a page, and Pages on a private repo needs a paid plan while the site is public anyway. Zero-hosting fallback: a GIF or screenshots in a README. Must confirm a run picks up nothing private before the first publish.
remediation: PROMOTED into #504 scope by the 2026 revision — WS-10: the run repo `cbartens/bkit-example` is already public, so GitHub Pages serves the built demo from its root (`https://cbartens.github.io/bkit-example/`) with no separate demo repo; the pre-first-publish private-content sweep is covered by the existing every-push privacy scan + manual review

Meeting planner across time zones: daylight saving silently moves the meeting an hour for one person — the most impressive catch, and works with no packages. Recipe scaler: scaling '1/3 cup' by 1.5 gives 0.4999999 — friendly but a weak story. summary: Warn at install when the issue tracker resolves to none in a repo created for the pipeline
description: Surfaced by the #504 risk premortem. DEFAULT_ISSUE_TRACKER is 'none' (install/manifest.ts:66), so `bkit install` without --tracker=github records issueTracker 'none' and every workflow renders '_No tracker connected, skip step._': no error, no gate, and a demo that narrates a pipeline which never touched the tracker — the highest-severity silent failure found. The example works around it with an explicit flag plus a preflight, but the underlying silent default remains for every other consumer.
remediation: consider a bkit install / `bkit doctor` advisory naming --tracker=github as the fix when issueTracker resolves to none; NOT a hard blocker, since a none-tracker consumer is legitimate

summary: PR-time capability-register enforcement via head-ref checkout job
description: The Check Capability Register gate runs on push events only: a pull_request checkout is the merge ref, whose tree can differ from the head the register was built against, so gating there is a false red no author can clear. A stale register can still merge to dev and red the push run; the correction is a docs-only bkit [skip ci] refresh. True pre-merge enforcement needs a job that checks out the PR head ref and runs pnpm graph:check against that tree. Declared an optional follow-up in the issue 444 O5 decision comment (Open risks).
remediation: add a pull_request job that checks out github.event.pull_request.head.sha and runs pnpm graph:check on that tree

summary: Verify graphify 0.9.50 ubuntu output matches the macOS-built register on the first CI run of the gate
description: Blocked on an ubuntu-latest CI runner executing the new Check Capability Register step; the local environment is macOS and cannot reproduce it. The committed register was built on macOS with graphify 0.9.50; if ubuntu output diverges the step is a false red on every dev push. Documented fallback: demote the step to advisory and gate on register-stamp freshness instead (issue 444 O5 decision comment, Open risks).
remediation: on the first push carrying the gate, check the bkit-tests-static lane Check Capability Register step on ubuntu-latest; if it reds on a byte diff, apply the documented fallback

summary: Run bkit against an external benchmark suite for industry-comparable numbers
description: The #504 external-tools survey (fact-checked: SlopCodeBench arXiv 2603.24755 and DeepSWE arXiv 2607.07946 are real) was considered and rejected for the example project on scope-mismatch grounds — those suites benchmark agent/model capability on their tasks, while the example benchmarks bkit orchestration on our task. Running bkit inside an external suite (SWE-bench-style or SCBench-style harness) would give industry-comparable numbers, but is a legitimately different exercise: containerised execution, hidden graders and per-task instrumentation the example deliberately avoids.
remediation: not this cycle; if revisited, treat it as a separate benchmark project that wraps bkit in an external harness rather than changing the example repo

summary: Release-PR mirror mode is adopted in bkit's own bkit-ci
description: A same-repo PR whose head is dev or release/* into the default branch reuses the dev push run: Decide Release Mirror in bkit-tests-scope sets mirror_push_run, and Mirror Push Run in the bkit-tests-check capstone copies the dev push run verdict. Wire staging primitives into bkit-modules.ts write call sites + add subprocess SIGTERM integration test

summary: Reason set to needs-decision: pick cross-check-before-seed vs accept one-time board noise
description: Same-key follow-up supplying the REQUIRED reason the original row omitted (.bkit/jsonl.md § Deferral Reason). Decision owed: (a) have the bootstrap seed fuzzy-match migrated SHIPPED summaries before seeding, so legacy plans do not re-appear as in-flight; or (b) accept the one-time noise and let operators append ABANDONED/SHIPPED rows by hand after migration. Option (b) is cheaper and matches the on-disk-first, tracker-optional design intent; option (a) costs a matching heuristic that can mis-merge unrelated features. Not adjudicated unjustified: it fails test 1 — the remediation is a design choice between two architectures, not a bounded edit.
remediation: either (a) have the bootstrap seed cross-check completed.md/roadmap.jsonl SHIPPED summaries for a fuzzy title match before seeding, or (b) accept the one-time noise and let operators append ABANDONED/SHIPPED rows by hand post-migration to clean the initial board (cheaper, matches on-disk-first tracker-optional design intent)
