summary: docs/plans/** artifacts still quote the pre-sweep headings and internal labels; the shipped-docs guard deliberately excludes them
description: Five 363 build-log artifacts quote `## Post-merge dev CI auto-routing (#363)` verbatim, and plan/design docs across docs/plans/ carry issue refs and retired ledger keys throughout. bkit-shipped-docs-refs.test.ts scans only the manifest corpus plus the docs/ payload, so the archived tree is out of scope by design.
remediation: leave archived artifacts alone unless they start being read as current doctrine — they are phase records, and rewriting them destroys the audit trail the ship bookkeeping depends on. If a sweep is ever wanted, scope it to headings only and never to the finding bodies.

summary: The 363 plan still lists the 4.10.0 -> 4.11.0 bump as a task, so a re-run re-applies what this cycle reverted
description: Plan task T12 and its execution checklist instruct bumping package.json and .bkit/version pinnedVersion, calling the bump a forward-only release tag. The bump was reverted and the rule recorded (version-bump-belongs-to-the-release-commit), but the plan is an archived artifact and was left unedited, so any resume or replay of that plan reintroduces it.
remediation: no edit to the archived plan; the durable guard is the decision row plus the release procedure. If plan replay ever becomes routine, teach the plan template that version bumps are release-commit-only.

summary: Reconciler/sweeper to recover a ship displaced out of the depth-1 GHA concurrency queue
description: GHA holds exactly one pending run per concurrency group; a third concurrent ship displaces the pending second. That PR stays green, open and merge-ready but never ships, and the displaced run executes no step so no bkit-authored notice, comment, label or ledger row can exist for it. #397 restates requirement 1 as met for N=2 only and accepts the N>=3 hole this cycle, because the allowlist ship discriminator removes the dominant eviction source (green dev CI entering the ship lane). The automated fix is an idempotent reconciler: sweep for green bkit:auto PRs with no in-flight ship and re-dispatch, riding the post-merge dev CI trigger #363 adds (which fires exactly when the ship lane frees).
remediation: future issue after #397 lands: bump cloud job permissions to actions: write; cap the sweeper hard (max one dispatch per sweep, reuse #363's MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS bounding); make the admission probe and the sweep predicate call ONE shared implementation, not two similar gh run list invocations; keep the predicate stack-agnostic (workflow filename, never a consumer-editable CI display name). Belongs with #260's single-flight/idempotent-dispatch substrate.

summary: Split bkit-cloud.yml into a light router plus a single-trigger-surface executor workflow — the deferred target shape for multi-producer dispatch
description: #397 records this as the right long-term shape and rejects it for this cycle. bkit-cloud.yml keeps both trigger surfaces but becomes a router (checkout + resolve, ending in gh workflow run bkit-cloud-run.yml -f phase -f fid -f arg); the new executor has ONE trigger surface with ONE payload shape, so its concurrency group is a literal string and the cross-surface same-FID gap stops existing rather than being closed. It is also the natural dispatch primitive #260 (milestone workstreams) and #324 (audit findings) both want to consume: adding a producer becomes adding a caller, not editing a concurrency expression. Rejected now as net-new shipped infra (new workflow file, manifest entry, template, advisory, actions: write bump, two-hop latency, doubled Actions run count) for a problem two expressions plus a resolver job cover.
remediation: revisit when #260 and #324 add the second and third dispatch producers; at that point #397's expression work becomes the thing this replaces. A dropped or 403 re-dispatch is a silent no-op for a whole phase, so the router needs its own dispatch-verify.

summary: External cross-runner mutex (orphan git ref or issue-label compare-and-swap) as a real distributed single-flight lock
description: #397 rejects this for its own scope. The file locks (.bkit/.dev.lock, docs/plans/*/logs/{FID}/.lock) are gitignored and runner-local, so they arbitrate nothing across GHA runners. A primitive that does survive would be a compare-and-swap on a dedicated orphan ref (git push origin <sha>:refs/bkit-locks/ship-global — GitHub ref creation is server-atomic) or an issue-label CAS tolerating the 422 as lock-held, with age-based stale reaping mirroring today's 30-min-idle rule. It closes both gaps without depending on any inferred GHA behaviour. Rejected because it introduces a DURABLE state surface whose lock survives a hard-killed runner with no guaranteed reaper (an if: always() step can still be skipped on hard cancellation) — a worse blast radius than an ephemeral file lock that vanishes with the VM — and because it would leave two independent lock layers to reconcile.
remediation: revisit only if #260's single-flight lock / leader election requirement lands first and wants to share a primitive; design the reaper before the acquirer.

description: CI lint guarding against `.agents/scripts`/`.agents/templates` source-literal re-introduction in `.bkit/core/engine`

The 3 hand-authored .claude/agents/utility-*.md (utility-harvest-friction, utility-new-release, utility-pre-release-check) have no .bkit/core/prompts/ source, are not in the bkit install manifest, and can never be reached by the .bkit/core/prompts/*.md glob, so #342 universal untrusted-input coverage excludes them by construction; at least utility-pre-release-check (reads CI output) and utility-harvest-friction (reads friction.jsonl) ingest attacker-influenceable text
remediation: open a follow-up issue deciding whether the 3 hand-authored agents belong in the untrusted-content threat model; if yes they need either a .bkit/core/prompts/ source or a second gate glob over .claude/agents/utility-*.md — do NOT hand-edit the mirrors

summary: Nothing detects that the cloud egress allowlist pasted into a Claude/Cursor dashboard is stale relative to what bkit generates
description: cloud.md renders a paste block a human copies into a vendor dashboard. When bkit's derived host set changes (new provider, new MCP host) the dashboard keeps the old value and the only symptom is an opaque harness timeout on the model call, not a network error. No surface can compare intended to actual because the allowlist lives in a web UI. #381 ships a stable fingerprint line in the paste block as the cheap half of the mitigation; detection is out of scope.
remediation: future issue: have the cloud bootstrap hook echo the expected allowlist fingerprint (and optionally probe reachability of one provider host) so a mismatch is visible in the cloud run log

summary: One generated allowlist artifact read at runtime by all three IDE surfaces is blocked by the Claude and OpenCode permission schemas, not by bkit design
description: The theoretical ideal is a single JSON artifact (tooling defaults + all registry hosts + consumer allowed-domains) that every surface reads at runtime, collapsing BKIT_SHIPPED_NETWORK_DOMAINS, the Cursor hook list and the WebFetch allow entries into reads of one file. Cursor already works this way via .cursor/allowlist.json. Claude permissions.allow requires a literal WebFetch(domain:...) string per host and OpenCode permission.bash requires a literal command glob per host, neither has a file-reference primitive, so the work would land for 1 of 3 surfaces. Recorded so it is not re-proposed without re-discovering the constraint.
remediation: revisit only if Claude Code or OpenCode ships a file-referenced permission source; most of the maintenance win is already captured by deriving the source list in #381

summary: jsonl.md lists workflow and step as required envelope fields, but manually-authored rows have no phase to name
description: Three live rows omit workflow (one also omits step): docs/decisions.jsonl and docs/knowledge.jsonl rows carrying step manual-investigation, and one docs/failures.jsonl row. The field table in .bkit/jsonl.md marks workflow and step as required (no ? suffix, unlike subagent? and model?), so the schema and the data disagree. .bkit/core/engine/audits/repo/ledger-integrity.test.ts therefore gates ts/kind/repo/bkitVersion only — backfilling a phase name would put invented data in a ledger that feeds the analysis pass.
remediation: pick one: mark workflow/step optional in the jsonl.md field table for manually-authored rows, or define an explicit sentinel (workflow: manual) and backfill the three rows, then widen the gate in .bkit/core/engine/audits/repo/ledger-integrity.test.ts to cover both fields.

summary: no width reduction for bkit-build Step 10 challenge-1/-2 or Step 11 challenge-reconcile
description: bkit-build Step 10 runs two adversarial challengers carrying different dimensions (bugs / security), so dropping -2 deletes security coverage outright rather than trimming a duplicate. Step 11 challenge-reconcile stays unconditional as a direct consequence: with both challengers always running there are always two reports to merge, so a 'skip when only one ran' condition never fires. Sensitive-path globs may only force challenge width up, never reduce it.
remediation: none wanted — revisit only if a future lens split makes one challenger genuinely redundant

summary: bkit-build Step 4 build-plan-current stays unconditional
description: The obvious skip is 'the plan commit is an ancestor of the base', but Step 2 branching off a stale origin/dev is exactly the case this step exists to catch — the candidate predicate would disable the guard on its own failure mode. Dropped from the candidate list by the issue's own audit.
remediation: none wanted

summary: applicability predicates for design Step 3 ideate-2 (optimal-tradeoff) and ideate-3 (risk premortem)
description: Both lenses are candidates in the issue's audit, but Step 3 is the first subagent-invoking step in bkit-design and its only input is the raw issue text in design-input.md — there is no upstream artifact to carry a predicate and no bash-countable signal. Decision needed between: (A) keep all three ideate lenses unconditional and drop them from scope, forgoing a two-invocation saving on bug-fix-shaped designs but adding no machinery and risking no silent loss of the risk lens; (B) split Step 3 into two waves — run ideate-1 alone, have it emit LegacyConstraint and NewRuntimeSurface flags, then conditionally fan out -2 and -3, which needs no new agent but serialises a step that is parallel today so the full-width path pays wall-clock; (C) add a cheap pre-Step-3 classifier subagent emitting both flags, which keeps the fan-out parallel but is net-new machinery the issue ruled out and spends one invocation to maybe save two. Plan recommends A and applies it as the default.
remediation: pick A, B or C at the plan's Gate 1 confirmation; only B and C reopen this as implementation work

summary: extend the status-hole detector beyond ship to design / plan / build / debug
description: .bkit/core/engine/checks/status-holes.ts models ship only: a frozen canonical step order, four path classifications (PATH_A / PATH_B / MERGED_ON_ENTRY / ABORTED) and per-path mandatory sets, all derived from bkit-ship.md. Once step-skipped rows exist across all five workflows the detector could read skips from the log instead of inferring them from absence, which is the strongest available argument for promoting it from advisory to gate. Plan-sized rather than mechanical: each of the other four workflows needs its own routing-branch model (debug's NORMAL/SOAK ladder and attempt loops, build's verify/challenge retry loops, plan's SPLIT branch, design's SPIKE and MILESTONE branches), a corpus sweep to seed each expected set from real runs, and a per-workflow fail-open-to-gate promotion policy — new machinery in a new module surface, not an edit to the existing one.
remediation: design a per-workflow path model + expected-set derivation, seed each from a status.jsonl corpus sweep, then promote per workflow behind its own fail-open window

summary: no ask-rate signal in the Cursor guardrails hook, so a consumer whose .cursor/allowlist.json is missing or corrupt has nothing concrete to paste into a bug report
description: Once #381 deletes SHIPPED_NETWORK_BASES, a missing or corrupt .cursor/allowlist.json makes the hook ask on every outbound curl/wget including github.com. That is the intended fail-safe, but the consumer sees only repeated prompts. An ask-rate or degraded-state signal was suggested during design review and deliberately declined before build started: guardrails.cjs runs on every command in an editor session and its managed block is byte-equal hash-gated, so adding output there is new runtime behaviour in a shipped drift-gated hook with its own review surface. The degraded state is already self-diagnosing because the ask message names .cursor/allowlist.json and bkit install, which is the runbook half that matters most.
remediation: future issue: if the ask-on-everything state proves confusing in practice, add a one-shot degraded-state notice to the hook behind its own review, or surface it from bkit check instead of from the hook

summary: Amend plan template Design-Missing Fallback for standalone plans
description: docs/templates/bkit-plan.md:45 tells a standalone plan to replace Narrative and Success Criteria with the MISSING string and not to fabricate either. Shipped precedent authors both from a complete issue-side statement of intent (docs/plans/202607/363-widen-bkit-cloud-trigger-plan.md:75-85), and this plan does the same under human confirmation at Gate 1. The two are in conflict and the divergence is currently decided per plan.
remediation: Decide once whether the fallback clause covers standalone plans with a complete issue-side statement of intent, then amend docs/templates/bkit-plan.md and any prompt that quotes the clause.
source: plan review merge - template divergence flagged by tightness lens

summary: Codex has no read-tier gate: private-key deny and .env ask are unenforced there, because the Codex file-read tool name is unverified
description: The Codex guardrail is registered on the shell tool (Bash) only. The other three hosts also gate READS -- deny on .pem/.p12/id_rsa, ask on .env and .env.* -- and Codex does not, so on that host an agent can read private-key material and secrets with no gate at all. The blocker is that the hook matcher keys on tool_name and the Codex docs consulted confirm only Bash as a tool name; the file-read tool name was not established. Registering a guessed matcher is worse than leaving it: the hook installs, exits 0 and silently never fires, which is a gate that proves only that it was asked for. The read-gates block in .bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.integration.test.ts § permissions-parity is scoped to claude/opencode/cursor for this reason.
remediation: Confirm the Codex file-read tool name against the Codex hooks documentation, add a second PreToolUse matcher in .codex/hooks.json pointing at guardrails.cjs, port decideRead from the Cursor twin, and extend the read-gates describe to four hosts. Deny is real on Codex, so the .pem tier enforces properly; the .env tier lands as advisory like the rest of the ask tier.

summary: opencode gates only through its permission table, so the shell-as-edit-channel gate and URL-host matching cannot be expressed on that host
description: Two gates the other three hosts carry are absent on opencode, both for the same structural reason: it has a glob-keyed permission table and no guardrails script. (1) Shell-as-edit-channel -- deciding whether a redirect target is a tracked source file or scratch needs the path parsed, which a glob cannot do; a blanket sed -i ask would prompt constantly and would also break the sanctioned bulk rewrite at bkit-plan.md:923. (2) URL-host matching -- its curl allows are substring-keyed, so curl https://evil.example/?src=github.com and curl https://github.com.attacker.io/ both match a github.com allow and read as allowlisted. Cursor parses the host correctly; Claude and Codex now do too.
remediation: Give opencode a guardrails plugin alongside its existing GateGuard plugin, reusing the shared decision engine, then extend the shell-as-edit-channel and host-matching describes in .bkit/core/engine/install/modules/index.integration.test.ts § permissions-parity to include it. Plan-sized rather than mechanical: opencode's plugin contract differs from both the Cursor beforeShellExecution shape and the Claude-family PreToolUse envelope, so it is a third adapter rather than a copy.

summary: Mode-3 (cloud, RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=false) BOOK_ROOT live-verification is not exercised in the ship bookkeeping E2E validation — both validated paths are local-mode (RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES=true)
description: Prose contract is mechanically asserted by the Tier-2 invariant (.bkit/core/engine/audits/workflows/ship-invariants.test.ts BOOK_ROOT conditional presence check) and the Failure Path checks in .bkit/core/engine/audits/workflows/ship-invariants.test.ts, but the live path is unexercised. Blocker: mode-3 requires a cloud agent (Claude Code cloud / Cursor cloud) executing a ship workflow, which is not available in a local build session; the three-runtimes RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES live verification it depends on is itself still OPEN. Supersedes the same-key row that carried this prose in a free-text reason field, no description, lowercase severity, a friction-only scope field, a non-schema dependsOn field and ts 0.
remediation: verify on the first mode-3 ship run: assert BOOK_ROOT resolves to the main checkout and the bookkeeping commit lands there, then close this row

summary: The 'start a new run?' test keys on the last run overall, not the last run of THIS workflow — an interleaved debug run can silently reset a resuming build's attempt budget
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. `bkit workflows start` (.bkit/src/commands/workflow/workflows.ts:420-421) tests `fold(...).at(-1)` — the last folded run of ANY workflow — to decide whether to append a fresh workflow-started row; runNumber (.bkit/src/bkit-status.ts:213-217) keys on the same `runs.at(-1)`. build and debug write to the SAME docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl. So if a debug run interleaves and completes between two build invocations, a resuming build sees the latest run's workflow == 'debug', appends a fresh workflow-started, and starts a NEW active run — resetting its attempt budget. #58 makes active-run scoping the basis of every counter, which promotes this from latent to load-bearing: it is Defect 3 (fresh budget on resume) through a side door, reachable via the exact build->debug->build path the feature governs. A lock exists (`bkit locks acquire`, .bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:189); whether it excludes the interleave is NOT established. Current behaviour is characterised in .bkit/src/commands/workflow/counters.test.ts:191 ('an interleaved debug run makes the paused build run count as finished') so the dependence is visible rather than latent; the boundary is unchanged.
remediation: Decide the intended run-boundary semantics and key the test on the last run OF THE SAME WORKFLOW (lastRun(runs, workflow) in .bkit/src/bkit-status.ts) rather than `.at(-1)` at workflows.ts:420-421 and bkit-status.ts:213-217, or establish and document that the bkit-build.md:189 lock makes the interleave impossible. Belongs with #209's status.jsonl substrate, not with #58's control-flow slice. Read counters.test.ts:191's characterisation assertion first — it records what today actually does.

summary: debug-run-tests writes its step-done row with no commit (KN-26 removed it), so NORMAL_ATTEMPT's row counting depends transitively on Steps 4/5/6 advancing parentSha
description: Surfaced by plan review of #58. Counters count step-done rows and the fold dedups on (workflow, step, parentSha, at) (.bkit/src/bkit-status.ts:62-66). build-run-tests commits per attempt via `bkit steps done` (.bkit/workflows/bkit-build.md:1120; --allow-empty at .bkit/src/commands/workflow/steps.ts:321), so its parentSha advances by itself. debug-run-tests does NOT (.bkit/workflows/bkit-debug.md:395 passes --commit=none — the only step-done-writing step in debug without a commit). That asymmetry is KN-26's remediation: a chore(...) commit as branch HEAD makes the Vercel-ignore regex skip the preview, CI demotes to partial, integration/Playwright are skipped, and the run reports conclusion=success with no coverage. So NORMAL_ATTEMPT's attempts stay distinct only via Steps 4/5/6's commits (bkit-debug.md:619/:700/:773) advancing parentSha, plus the dedup key's 'at' second. Whether debug-run-tests SHOULD regain a commit — making its row counting self-sufficient — is a real design question that collides with KN-26 and must not be settled by an implementer applying #58's per-site shape. The current shape is pinned by a corpus audit (.bkit/src/bkit-counter-prose-audit.test.ts:248 TRANSITIVE_EXEMPTIONS) that requires each counted step to either commit in-block or sit on the transitive-exemption list.
remediation: If debug-run-tests's transitive parentSha dependency proves fragile, resolve it WITHOUT re-adding a chore(...) commit — e.g. amend the dedup key, or have the step commit under a subject the Vercel-ignore regex does not match. Any change must be reviewed against KN-26's full failure chain first. Do not simply delete the TRANSITIVE_EXEMPTIONS entry (.bkit/src/bkit-counter-prose-audit.test.ts:248).

summary: GitHub merge queue (rebase onto base, CI on merge_group, server-side merge if green) is unavailable to bkit consumers — private + non-Enterprise; would require a merge_group trigger in every consumer ci.yml
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. A GitHub merge queue would make the merge gate server-side (rebase onto base, run CI on the merge_group event, auto-merge if green) and remove the head-movement race `bkit runs gate` (.bkit/src/commands/workflow/runs.ts:1368) exists to close. Unavailable: bkit consumer repos (consumer-a, consumer-b) are private and on a non-Enterprise plan; merge_group is an Enterprise/Beta feature gated behind plan tier. Adopting it would require every consumer ci.yml to add a merge_group trigger and the repos to upgrade their plan — a cross-consumer policy change, not a ship-workflow decision.
remediation: revisit only if the consumer plan tier changes (private repos gain merge queue access); record the plan-tier gate in docs/deployments.md alongside the merge-gate contract when revisited

summary: Required status checks on dev via `bkit setup protect-main` (closing the UI hand-merge path) — separable additive cross-consumer policy with its own plan-tier question; deferred from #384 ship gate
description: #384 Out-of-Scope mirror. `bkit setup protect-main` (.bkit/src/commands/setup/setup.ts:39, BRANCH = "main") already makes bkit-tests-check the sole required check on main; its header (setup.ts:6-8) states dev is left unprotected on purpose — operators choose direct-push or feat/PR. Extending required-status-checks enforcement to dev (so a human cannot UI-merge a PR whose capstone is not green, closing the gap `bkit runs gate` closes on the agent path) is a separable additive policy. It has its own plan-tier question: branch protection on private repos is plan-gated (the REST protection/ruleset APIs return 403 on cbartens/bkit today — see docs/deployments.md § Autonomous phase-close prerequisites), so the enforcement cannot be verified mechanically on every consumer. Out of scope for #384 because the agent-driven gate (`bkit runs gate`, .bkit/src/commands/workflow/runs.ts:1368) is the load-bearing assertion; UI-merge prevention is defence-in-depth, not the contract.
remediation: future issue: extend `bkit setup protect-main` (.bkit/src/commands/setup/setup.ts) to dev (or a ruleset), reconciling the setup.ts:6-8 'dev left unprotected on purpose' stance, and document the plan-tier prerequisite; pair with per-workflow-rollback-path-for-shipped-bkit-workflow-changes if that affordance lands first

summary: OpenCode curl/wget allowlist is a command substring glob, so an allowlisted domain in a query param or header defeats the host check Cursor now enforces
description: injectOpencodeDerivedAllows writes permission.bash entries of the form 'curl *{base}*' (bkit-modules.ts:1899-1911). OpenCode's permission model is a command glob, so 'curl https://evil.tld/?x=z.ai' matches and is allowed, while the Cursor hook rejects it (host-parsed since #394) and Claude has no shell curl gate at all. #381 widens the base list and therefore widens this asymmetry; it documents the weaker guarantee in .bkit/providers.md rather than fixing it, because OpenCode exposes no URL-host permission primitive.
remediation: future issue: revisit if OpenCode gains a host-based permission primitive or a pre-tool hook comparable to Cursor beforeShellExecution; until then keep the limitation stated in providers.md

summary: bkit uninstall deletes derived WebFetch grants by recomputing resolveNetworkAllowlist, so it cannot distinguish a hand-added grant that collides with a derived base
description: Corrected premise, verified against source 2026-08-26. .bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts:550-562 recomputes resolveClaudeDerivedAllows(ctx.cwd) at :556 and folds it into templateDoc.permissions.allow BEFORE stripTier2JsonScope, so enrich-added grants were never scoped to the .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json seed and emptying that seed strands nothing. The real gap is the inverse: uninstall deletes by RECOMPUTATION rather than by provenance, so any permissions.allow entry matching the CURRENT derived set is treated as bkit-owned and removed, including one the consumer added by hand. #381 widens the derived set from 10 to 15 bases (githubcopilot.com, models.dev, npmjs.org, skills.sh, tavily.com), widening that strip scope by 10 entries. PLAN-SIZED because the uninstall decision matrix is format-driven (fully-managed, markered-text, byte-equal-text, json) and consuming provenance adds a fourth axis that every format branch and the heavy-customised-consumer round-trip byte-identity fixture must be re-reasoned against; it is the same class of change as #381's WebFetch prune, on a different verb.
remediation: future issue: read .bkit/version claudeAllowDerived (the record #381 introduces) in bkit-uninstall.ts instead of recomputing resolveClaudeDerivedAllows at :556, and strip exactly the strings bkit recorded writing; add a round-trip integration case asserting a hand-added non-derived grant survives bkit uninstall claude while derived grants do not

summary: OpenCode permission.bash curl/wget allow globs are never revoked on any verb, so a dropped allowed-domains entry keeps its shell egress grant forever
description: injectOpencodeDerivedAllows (.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1899-1911) assigns bash[`curl *${base}*`] = allow and bash[`wget *${base}*`] = allow for every resolved base and deletes nothing, on install or upgrade. The injected keys are absent from the rendered template, so stripTier2JsonScope leaves them on uninstall too. A consumer who removes a domain from .agents/context.md allowed-domains loses WebFetch(domain:<d>) via #381's prune and keeps curl *<d>* and wget *<d>* permanently: a shell egress grant strictly broader than the WebFetch grant that was revoked. #381 adds ten more such keys per consumer (five new bases x curl + wget) and does not close this. Distinct from 381-opencode-curl-glob-substring-bypass, which covers the glob SHAPE (a query parameter defeats the substring match) and not the LIFECYCLE. PLAN-SIZED because closing it needs a second provenance record for .opencode/opencode.json with no .bkit/version analogue today, a second recording contract mirroring #381's dryRun and non-writing-path rules, and an uninstall interaction of its own on a surface that install merges rather than rewrites.
remediation: future issue: give .opencode/opencode.json the same previous-minus-current prune #381 gives .claude/settings.json, recording the injected glob keys in .bkit/version alongside claudeAllowDerived; or define one revocation contract every egress surface implements and assert it with a single cross-surface parity test

description: #381 removes the domain-list duplication but not the key-set duplication: OPENCODE_PROVIDER_DEFAULTS (bkit-registry.ts:36) is mirrored by OPENCODE_PROVIDERS + OPENCODE_PROVIDER_ALIASES (bkit-cli.ts:30-76), GATEWAY_COLUMN (bkit-install.ts:303), EFFORT_COLUMN_FOR_PROGRAM (bkit-install.ts:444), and the Models tables in .bkit/prompts.md and .bkit/providers.md. bkit-cli.ts:27 carries the same 'keep in sync with ...' comment pattern #381 exists to remove, and no test asserts key-set parity. Out of scope for #381, which is scoped to egress hosts.

summary: bkit upgrade does not write .bkit/advisories.md, so an advisory raised on the upgrade path has no durable artifact
description: writeAdvisoriesArtifact is called only from the doctor branch (bkit-install.ts:1874) and the install/check path (bkit-install.ts:2757); the upgrade branch returns without it. #381 adds a webfetch-grants-pruned advisory naming the exact WebFetch(domain:...) strings it removed, so on upgrade only two of the three recording destinations apply: the console line and git diff .claude/settings.json. This is a general install/upgrade finalisation-parity gap that pre-dates #381 and affects every advisory, not just the prune's. PLAN-SIZED because closing it means restructuring where the upgrade branch finalises and flushes ctx.advisories, not adding a call at the existing return: the install path builds its finding set through runPostInstallCheck, which upgrade never enters, so the fix is a new shared finalisation seam plus its cross-verb parity coverage.
remediation: future issue: restructure the upgrade branch's finalisation so it flushes its findings through the same runPostInstallCheck plus writeAdvisoriesArtifact path install uses, then assert parity with an integration test that raises one advisory on each verb

If a new ship merge gate is wrong, the recovery path for three consumer repos is currently undefined. 384 mitigates locally with a single logged override (BKIT_SHIP_GATE_OVERRIDE recorded as a status.jsonl row), but that is a per-run escape, not a rollback.

summary: Do not fold #384 into #341 — sequence ship redesign after runtime-aware close lands
description: #384 (Path A read-only resume / Path B integrate-then-revalidate, one capstone gate, bookkeeping on the dev tree) layers on #341 rather than conflicting. #341 makes ship runtime-aware (where the tree is, whether RUNTIME_DEVPUSHES); #384 makes ship head-stable (what may move the PR head). summary: Reconciler/sweeper to recover a ship displaced out of the depth-1 GHA concurrency queue
description: GHA holds exactly one pending run per concurrency group; a third concurrent ship displaces the pending second. That PR stays green, open and merge-ready but never ships, and the displaced run executes no step so no bkit-authored notice, comment, label or ledger row can exist for it. #397 restates requirement 1 as met for N=2 only and accepts the N>=3 hole this cycle, because the allowlist ship discriminator removes the dominant eviction source (green dev CI entering the ship lane). The automated fix is an idempotent reconciler: sweep for green bkit:auto PRs with no in-flight ship and re-dispatch, riding the post-merge dev CI trigger #363 adds (which fires exactly when the ship lane frees).
remediation: future issue after #397 lands: bump cloud job permissions to actions: write; cap the sweeper hard (max one dispatch per sweep, reuse #363's MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS bounding); make the admission probe and the sweep predicate call ONE shared implementation, not two similar gh run list invocations; keep the predicate stack-agnostic (workflow filename, never a consumer-editable CI display name). Belongs with #260's single-flight/idempotent-dispatch substrate.

summary: Split bkit-cloud.yml into a light router plus a single-trigger-surface executor workflow — the deferred target shape for multi-producer dispatch
description: #397 records this as the right long-term shape and rejects it for this cycle. bkit-cloud.yml keeps both trigger surfaces but becomes a router (checkout + resolve, ending in gh workflow run bkit-cloud-run.yml -f phase -f fid -f arg); the new executor has ONE trigger surface with ONE payload shape, so its concurrency group is a literal string and the cross-surface same-FID gap stops existing rather than being closed. It is also the natural dispatch primitive #260 (milestone workstreams) and #324 (audit findings) both want to consume: adding a producer becomes adding a caller, not editing a concurrency expression. Rejected now as net-new shipped infra (new workflow file, manifest entry, template, advisory, actions: write bump, two-hop latency, doubled Actions run count) for a problem two expressions plus a resolver job cover.
remediation: revisit when #260 and #324 add the second and third dispatch producers; at that point #397's expression work becomes the thing this replaces. A dropped or 403 re-dispatch is a silent no-op for a whole phase, so the router needs its own dispatch-verify.

summary: External cross-runner mutex (orphan git ref or issue-label compare-and-swap) as a real distributed single-flight lock
description: #397 rejects this for its own scope. The file locks (.bkit/.dev.lock, docs/plans/*/logs/{FID}/.lock) are gitignored and runner-local, so they arbitrate nothing across GHA runners. A primitive that does survive would be a compare-and-swap on a dedicated orphan ref (git push origin <sha>:refs/bkit-locks/ship-global — GitHub ref creation is server-atomic) or an issue-label CAS tolerating the 422 as lock-held, with age-based stale reaping mirroring today's 30-min-idle rule. It closes both gaps without depending on any inferred GHA behaviour. Rejected because it introduces a DURABLE state surface whose lock survives a hard-killed runner with no guaranteed reaper (an if: always() step can still be skipped on hard cancellation) — a worse blast radius than an ephemeral file lock that vanishes with the VM — and because it would leave two independent lock layers to reconcile.
remediation: revisit only if #260's single-flight lock / leader election requirement lands first and wants to share a primitive; design the reaper before the acquirer.

summary: With ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENCODE_PROVIDER_KEY both set, one bkit-cloud run launches two agents that both dispatch /bkit-auto against the same PR
description: The claude and opencode jobs are additive by design and documented as such in the bkit-cloud.yml header: both fire on the same event when both secrets are present. They are ONE run, so workflow-level concurrency cannot separate them by construction — a ship-global lane delivers one ship RUN at a time, not one ship AGENT at a time. Two agents then race on the same feat/{FID} branch and the same PR, backstopped only by gh pr merge --match-head-commit. #397 leaves this exactly as today: its job-level FID lanes are suffixed per agent (-claude / -opencode) precisely so the additive contract is not silently converted into a queue with its own eviction hazard. Pre-existing, not introduced by #397, and simultaneously an intended feature and an unarbitrated same-FID collision.
remediation: future issue: decide whether additive dual-agent execution is still wanted post-#397; if yes, scope it to non-mutating phases or give the two agents disjoint worktrees; if no, make the jobs mutually exclusive at the secret-gate step rather than via a shared concurrency group.

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers API-contract conformance — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded, and invisible once Pass 2 became historical

Pass 3 said nothing about it and Pass 4 folded no probe for it, so the 18-lens inventory silently has no coverage of published-interface breakage, schema drift between producer and consumer, or endpoint contract regressions. The defer is still the right call — the gap is that the RATIONALE stopped being visible the moment Passes 2 and 3 were reclassified as historical and the Pass-4 doc became the sole input to /bkit-plan. That is the same failure shape that lost the WS-1..WS-8 decomposition when sub-issues 187-193 and 208 were deleted.
remediation: do NOT add a lens without first reading this row — it has now been deferred twice on the same signal-to-noise argument. Candidate home is WS-E (#83) once runtime evidence exists and a real surface can be diffed, or a conditional lens gated on a new hasPublicApi flag authored in WS-C. Not 4.11.0.

summary: No lens in the /bkit-audit 18 covers rate limiting / abuse throttling — deferred in Pass 2, never re-recorded
description: Pass 2 deferred a rate-limiting lens alongside api-contracts on the same argument. Pass 4 carries no probe for request throttling, quota enforcement, backoff on retry paths, or abuse surfaces, and the security lens (B9) is chartered to hunt permissive holes in auth, validation, secrets and data exposure rather than request-rate policy. Verified absent under every synonym (rate-limit, throttl, quota, backoff, abuse). The defer stands: detecting a MISSING rate limit needs request-path modelling that a static grep-shaped lens does not do, and a false negative here reads as a clean security pass.
remediation: candidate homes are WS-E (#83, once a live surface can be probed) or an amendment to security (B9) — but only with a probe that can distinguish absent-limit from limit-enforced-at-a-layer-not-in-this-repo, otherwise it emits confident false negatives on exactly the class it exists to catch. Not 4.11.0.

summary: derived-data (C3) absorbs only the CONSISTENCY half of Pass-2 deferred caching lens — TTL, invalidation, stampede and key-cardinality remain uncovered by all 18
description: Pass 2 deferred a caching lens. Pass 4 introduces derived-data (C3, gated on hasDerivedStore), which covers cache CONSISTENCY: single-authoritative-writer, every source-mutation path updating the derived store, and whether any test or store constraint asserts the two agree. It does NOT cover cache CORRECTNESS or EFFICIENCY: TTL policy, invalidation strategy, stampede / thundering-herd protection, or key-cardinality blowup. The risk is a reader treating the Pass-2 caching defer as fully resolved because a cache-shaped lens now exists, when only one half was absorbed — the partial absorption is easy to mistake for a complete one.
remediation: if the caching half is wanted, it is an amendment to derived-data (C3) rather than a new lens — same hasDerivedStore gate, same subject identity — but it changes the lens from a consistency derivation into a policy scan, so decide deliberately rather than by accretion. Not 4.11.0.

summary: main branch excluded from the bkit-cloud workflow_run trigger — a documented REVERSAL of #363 pivot-comment D-final, which settled the branch filter as [feat/**, fix/**, dev, main]
description: #363's pivot comment (2026-07-22) D-final explicitly listed 'verify at both dev (post-merge) and main (post dev->main promotion)' with a routing table and diff both including main. The plan (v3/v4) moved main to Out of Scope instead, and this build ships without it. summary: MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS cap is enforced from status.jsonl on origin/dev, a file the dispatched /bkit-debug session itself has contents:write to rewrite — the cap is self-resettable by the principal it bounds
description: bkit-cloud.yml documents MAX_DEV_DISPATCH_ATTEMPTS=3 as a cost/security control bounding a stuck dev/fix/** feedback loop, but the counter it reads (dev-dispatch rows in docs/plans/{YYYYMM}/logs/{FID}/status.jsonl on origin/dev) is the same file every dispatched /bkit-debug session legitimately edits every run, with contents:write. Any actor or malfunctioning/prompt-injected agent that can push to dev can rewrite or drop those rows, silently restoring the remaining-attempts budget to 3 and continuing the failure->debug->push->failure cycle indefinitely. The fail-closed push-verification added for #363 P6 protects only against under-counting from lost pushes, not against an authorized rewrite.
remediation: Derive the count from a source the dispatched session cannot rewrite — e.g. gh run list --workflow bkit-cloud.yml filtered by FID, or an append-only tracker comment/label written with a token the dispatched session does not hold — or minimally cross-check the file-derived count against gh api run history and take the maximum before dispatching. summary: One vocabulary for conditional-lens outcomes across workflows and audit
description: Two surfaces are converging on the same idea with different names. summary: Drift gate over the rendered host mirrors
description: The rendered agent and command mirrors under .claude, .cursor and .opencode are force-overwritten and untracked by the drift check, so bkit check exits 0 while a mirror is stale against its source. A source edit that is never re-rendered therefore ships silently, and agents act on the stale rendered copy. Plan-sized rather than a mechanical fix: it needs a per-host render-output model (what each host emits for a given source, including the prune set), a decision on whether force-overwritten output can be drift-gated at all without fighting the overwrite, and a fail-open to gate promotion policy so the first release does not block on pre-existing drift.
remediation: Model the render output per host, add a drift comparison for it, and land it fail-open for one release before promoting to a gate.

summary: bkit upgrade does not write .bkit/advisories.md, so an advisory raised on the upgrade path has no durable artifact
description: writeAdvisoriesArtifact is called only from the doctor branch (bkit-install.ts:1874) and the install/check path (bkit-install.ts:2757); the upgrade branch returns without it. #381 adds a webfetch-grants-pruned advisory naming the exact WebFetch(domain:...) strings it removed, so on upgrade only two of the three recording destinations apply: the console line and git diff .claude/settings.json. This is a general install/upgrade finalisation-parity gap that pre-dates #381 and affects every advisory, not just the prune's. PLAN-SIZED because closing it means restructuring where the upgrade branch finalises and flushes ctx.advisories, not adding a call at the existing return: the install path builds its finding set through runPostInstallCheck, which upgrade never enters, so the fix is a new shared finalisation seam plus its cross-verb parity coverage.
remediation: future issue: restructure the upgrade branch's finalisation so it flushes its findings through the same runPostInstallCheck plus writeAdvisoriesArtifact path install uses, then assert parity with an integration test that raises one advisory on each verb

summary: bkit uninstall deletes derived WebFetch grants by recomputing resolveNetworkAllowlist, so it cannot distinguish a hand-added grant that collides with a derived base
description: Corrected premise, verified against source 2026-08-26. .bkit/src/bkit-uninstall.ts:550-562 recomputes resolveClaudeDerivedAllows(ctx.cwd) at :556 and folds it into templateDoc.permissions.allow BEFORE stripTier2JsonScope, so enrich-added grants were never scoped to the .bkit/templates/.claude/settings.json seed and emptying that seed strands nothing. The real gap is the inverse: uninstall deletes by RECOMPUTATION rather than by provenance, so any permissions.allow entry matching the CURRENT derived set is treated as bkit-owned and removed, including one the consumer added by hand. #381 widens the derived set from 10 to 15 bases (githubcopilot.com, models.dev, npmjs.org, skills.sh, tavily.com), widening that strip scope by 10 entries. PLAN-SIZED because the uninstall decision matrix is format-driven (fully-managed, markered-text, byte-equal-text, json) and consuming provenance adds a fourth axis that every format branch and the heavy-customised-consumer round-trip byte-identity fixture must be re-reasoned against; it is the same class of change as #381's WebFetch prune, on a different verb.
remediation: future issue: read .bkit/version claudeAllowDerived (the record #381 introduces) in bkit-uninstall.ts instead of recomputing resolveClaudeDerivedAllows at :556, and strip exactly the strings bkit recorded writing; add a round-trip integration case asserting a hand-added non-derived grant survives bkit uninstall claude while derived grants do not

summary: no ask-rate signal in the Cursor guardrails hook, so a consumer whose .cursor/allowlist.json is missing or corrupt has nothing concrete to paste into a bug report

That is the intended fail-safe, but the consumer sees only repeated prompts. An ask-rate or degraded-state signal was suggested during design review and deliberately declined before build started: guardrails.cjs runs on every command in an editor session and its managed block is byte-equal hash-gated, so adding output there is new runtime behaviour in a shipped drift-gated hook with its own review surface. The degraded state is already self-diagnosing because the ask message names .cursor/allowlist.json and bkit install, which is the runbook half that matters most.
remediation: future issue: if the ask-on-everything state proves confusing in practice, add a one-shot degraded-state notice to the hook behind its own review, or surface it from bkit check instead of from the hook

summary: OpenCode permission.bash curl/wget allow globs are never revoked on any verb, so a dropped allowed-domains entry keeps its shell egress grant forever
description: injectOpencodeDerivedAllows (.bkit/src/bkit-modules.ts:1899-1911) assigns bash[`curl *${base}*`] = allow and bash[`wget *${base}*`] = allow for every resolved base and deletes nothing, on install or upgrade. The injected keys are absent from the rendered template, so stripTier2JsonScope leaves them on uninstall too. A consumer who removes a domain from .agents/context.md allowed-domains loses WebFetch(domain:<d>) via #381's prune and keeps curl *<d>* and wget *<d>* permanently: a shell egress grant strictly broader than the WebFetch grant that was revoked. #381 adds ten more such keys per consumer (five new bases x curl + wget) and does not close this. Distinct from 381-opencode-curl-glob-substring-bypass, which covers the glob SHAPE (a query parameter defeats the substring match) and not the LIFECYCLE. PLAN-SIZED because closing it needs a second provenance record for .opencode/opencode.json with no .bkit/version analogue today, a second recording contract mirroring #381's dryRun and non-writing-path rules, and an uninstall interaction of its own on a surface that install merges rather than rewrites.
remediation: future issue: give .opencode/opencode.json the same previous-minus-current prune #381 gives .claude/settings.json, recording the injected glob keys in .bkit/version alongside claudeAllowDerived; or define one revocation contract every egress surface implements and assert it with a single cross-surface parity test

remediation: Stop truncating the compared key (hash the full key, or truncate a digest of it), then re-derive and re-run the prune gate over the existing store rows.
